News.title: I posed as a migrant to cross the Channel in a dinghy – French cops are giving people smugglers free lifts back to camps
News.content:
AN undercover reporter was able to cross the Channel in a small boat while posing as a migrant – and claims French police are giving smugglers free lifts back to the camps.

Journalist Christian Drogan spent weeks posing as a British criminal who was on the run in Calais before boarding a UK-bound dinghy.



Working alongside Isabel Oakeshott from Talk TV, Drogan filmed his route back to the UK, including his interactions with the criminal gangs who have control over the route.

He says it was obvious who the smugglers behind the illegal crossings were “without a shadow of a doubt” – but French police did not arrest them.



Footage shows Drogan boarding an inflatable in shallow waters on the northern French coast along with dozens of migrants.

After setting off on relatively calm seas, footage shows a Gendarmerie patrol boat approaching the dinghy.

Officers are then heard saying in English: “The sea is very rough, here it is quiet, when you go further it’s very dangerous.

“The best way today is to go back.”



Drogan said the French police offered to take anyone back to shore if they had changed their mind about crossing.

He claims the four smugglers were the only people to accept the offer – and were dropped back on the beach to continue the work of their criminal network organising the journeys.

He says it took seven hours for his boat to reach the halfway point to Britain.



Drogan, a 35-year-old builder from Rochdale, has previously spent weeks undercover inside migrant camps in Calais.

He posed under different cover stories, including as a Kurd, an Armenian, and a small-time British criminal.

Once the dinghy had reached British waters, Drogan’s footage shows Border Force workers helping migrants onto a rescue vessel.

He says at this point it became obvious to the authorities that he was not a genuine migrant.

One worker told him: “You’re on the wrong boat”.



Drogan was then taken to Western Jet Foil in Dover where small boat migrants are processed.

He said at that point he was singled out and quizzed by counter terror cops about what he had seen.

Official Home Office statistics show that on the day the reporter crossed the Channel, August 3, one boat was picked up by Border Force carrying 35 people.

So far this year 15,897 people have arrived in the UK having crossed illegally from France – which is 43.8 per cent lower than this time last year.

It is not known if Drogan’s undercover journey has been counted in the official migrant arrival figures.



The Government claimed Drogan had been “reckless” and had “made it more difficult for law enforcement officers to stop small boat crossings and save lives in dangerous conditions”.

A Home Office spokesperson said: “Our partnership with France is stronger than ever, with a new deal signed by the Home Secretary delivering a 40% uplift in boots on the ground.

“Together, we are piling the pressure on the criminal gangs and preventing illegal and dangerous crossings.

“Over 1,100 boats or engines have been seized since the election, 48,000 crossing attempts have been prevented, and the number of small boats crossings are down.”

Last week footage released by the Home Office showed French police being attacked by migrants before they managed to successfully slash a dinghy as it was being launched.



Oakeshott said: “There is a very good reason no reporter has ever attempted such a mission before: because it is both extraordinarily difficult, and extraordinarily dangerous.

“Getting to the truth of what is really happening in the Channel simply isn’t possible from the safety of the beaches.”

Drogan said: “I rolled the dice with my life for this investigation, and its findings have only cemented my scepticism towards the establishment.

“This type of investigation is dangerous, but so are the people running our country.

“Truth is the most effective weapon in this fight, and that is why this kind of work has to be done.”



Drogan warned against anyone trying to copy his trip.

He continued: “I would say if anybody tries to have a go at this, It’s highly likely they could end up dead.

“France has changed since even only just sort of a year ago when I started going over.

“It’s highly highly hostile now. It feels in places like a war zone.”

News.title: Afghan man, 24, charged with rape of girl, 17, in UK city centre during early hours
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'HORROR ATTACK' Afghan man, 24, charged with rape of girl, 17, in UK city centre during early hours

COPS have charged an Afghan man after a 17-year-old girl was allegedly raped in a chilling city centre attack.

Abdul Shinwari, 24, has been charged following reports the teenager was attacked in Manchester.

The alleged rape happened on Hope Street, near Piccadilly Gardens, at around 1.30am on July 14.

Shinwari, of no fixed abode, has been charged with two counts of rape and two counts of sexual assault.





He also faces charges of non-fatal strangulation and possession with intent to supply.

The 24-year-old is due to appear at Manchester Crown Court today, Greater Manchester Police said.

Specialist safeguarding officers are continuing to support the teenage victim.

Police have not released further details about the alleged attack.

News.title: Man seriously injured and two hurt after brawl involving ‘bladed article’ in UK city centre – as two arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BLADE CHAOS Man seriously injured and two hurt after brawl involving ‘bladed article’ in UK city centre – as two arrested

A MAN has been seriously injured and two others hurt after a “large” city centre brawl involving a “bladed article”.

Cops have arrested two men following the violent clash, which saw armed cops swarm to the scene.



Police said that the violence broke out on Calenick Street in Truro at around 1.45pm.

The force added that one man suffered a “potentially serious injury” in the fracas.



Two others were left with minor injuries.

Police confirmed that two men, both in their 20s, have been arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm with intent.

The force said those involved are believed to have known each other.

A number of witnesses told CornwallLive there was an extremely large police and ambulance presence in the area.

One person said: “[The road is] all cordoned off around Burger King, around 30 coppers, 12 police cars”.

A force spokesperson said there was “no wider threat to the public”.



They added: “Those involved are believed to be known to each other and there is no wider threat to the public.”

Officers are now appealing for witnesses and anyone with relevant footage to come forward.

Anybody with information is urged to get in touch with the force, quoting 50260226230.

News.title: Trump launches ‘Operation Economic Outcast’ on Iran as he tries to isolate regime with damaging new sanctions
News.content:
DONALD Trump has launched his crushing “Operation Economic Outcast” on Iran by threatening crippling sanctions on any country propping up the regime.

The US president last week vowed to unleash the “MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN” to strong-arm Tehran into accepting his peace terms.



Washington has now upped the ante with a new plan to slap severe sanctions on any country maintaining economic ties with the regime.

Iran has meanwhile vowed it will retaliate against any country participating in the US-led isolation campaign.



With the war dragging on to the six-month mark, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced “Operation Economic Outcast” as a “warning shot” to Iran‘s allies.

Bessent said that the US was giving them a chance to “remedy bad behaviour” but stopped short of naming specific countries or laying out a timeline.



“Today, in that same spirit, we are launching an economic onslaught against Iran’s financial connections around the globe,” he said.

“Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone.”

Bessent declined to answer whether the move would target China, which bought 80 per cent of Iran’s ship oil last year.

But he said: “We want to make clear here today that no one is above the reach of US sanctions.



“That if they facilitate transactions and are part of the ecosystem that turns Iranian oil into money, into repression, they will be targeted.”

Bessent said that the US had identified countries who continued to deal with Iran and would set individual deadlines to cut off ties or face sanctions.

He added: “Any entity that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system. The clock just started ticking.”



Trump, he said, was making direct calls to world leaders to request that they “cease their interactions with the regime”.

Bessent did not elaborate on whether Trump had spoken with Xi Jinping after a successful summit in Beijing last month.

China’s embassy in Washington told reporters: “Regarding the ​Iran issue, sanctions and pressure do not help resolve the problem.

“China calls on the relevant parties to take responsible actions and resolve the issue through political and diplomatic means.”

Xi is set to meet Trump in Washington in late September, but fresh sanctions could sour prospects for extending a deal struck last November to keep Chinese rare earths flowing and cap US tariffs.



Iran brushed the sanctions off with the country’s finance minister saying it was “fully prepared” for them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ali Madanizadeh also accused the US of wanting to “wage economic terrorism”.

“We know how to play this game. This time, they should not think our response will be purely defensive and that we will only defend ourselves.”

News.title: Ukraine gives Britain ‘goldmine’ of secret battlefield data to help build AI weapons & protect bases from Russian spies
News.content:
UKRAINE has given Britain access to a treasure trove of top secret battlefield data to develop new AI weapons and protect bases from Russian attacks.

It comes as the UK granted Kyiv the blueprints to Storm Shadow long-range missiles, sparking a furious reproach from Vladimir Putin and his Kremlin warmongers.



Andy Burnham has now struck a deal with Volodymyr Zelensky to use Ukraine‘s coveted Avengers AI Labs, which holds millions of pieces of real-life combat data gathered from the war.

The UK will become the first foreign country to access thousands of cameras and infrared sensors that have tracked Russian tanks, troops, artillery, air defences and drones, creating a “goldmine” for training AI.



The Ukrainian military said its systems are now capable of detecting 70 per cent of all Russian targets after combing through years of data collected throughout the war.

British scientists and tech firms will now be able to use the data to develop cutting-edge defence technology.



And the first system is already about to be deployed at a UK military site to spot protesters and hostile spies trying to gain intelligence.

It turns buried fibre-optic cables into giant AI-powered sensors and could eventually be used to protect airports, prisons, railways and power stations.

Britain will in return give Ukraine access to its universities, researchers and tech firms to help Kyiv develop new battlefield technology.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: “By combining the UK’s world-leading scientists, engineers and tech companies with Ukraine’s unique battlefield experience and data, we will strengthen both of our nations’ defence and security.”



The deal could also “revolutionise all parts of public life, from air traffic control to train systems,” the Ministry of Defence said.

Until now, British defence companies have relied on Ukrainian drone operations posted online, which offer just a snapshot of drone strikes and surveillance missions.

It comes at a crucial time for the UK, with Moscow orchestrating a series of surveillance operations on European military bases and nuclear sites.



Britain has also been targeted by drones trying to access sensitive facilities with drones launched from its shadow fleet vessels.

The UK and Ukraine are also collaborating on a second project to build low-power AI chips that could create more durable and intelligent drones and robotics.

Burnham hailed the “ground-breaking partnership” as he visited Kyiv on his first foreign trip as Prime Minister.

He said: “Ukraine has become one of the world’s leading innovators in defence technology, forged through courage, ingenuity and the hard lessons of war.”

The PM said the deal will give Britain “the opportunity to develop the technologies of the future, changing lives here in Britain and saving lives on the battlefield in Ukraine.”



It comes as Russia has accused the UK of “participating” in the war and warned that there would be “consequences” over supplying weapons to Ukraine.

Kremlin mouthpiece Dmitry Peskov blasted Britain for “adding fuel to the fire” for giving Zelensky information on the components on Storm Shadow missiles so that Kyiv can manufacture the weapon itself.

But Burnham hit back and said: “Who started the fire? That’s the question, isn’t it?”



Foreign minister Sergei Lavrov said that Russia would target and “destroy” facilities producing the missiles.

It comes amid mounting pressure on Putin’s war machine.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ukrainian forces have repeatedly pummelled the nation’s equivalent of Amazon and are systemically blasting apart their fuel hubs.

For a third night in a row, Ukrainian drones have blitzed Ozon, Russia’s second-biggest online retailer, in an attempt to bleed Putin‘s war chest dry.

News.title: Council house tenants face the boot if they live in squalor and neglect their gardens, Reform warns
News.content:
COUNCIL house tenants could be given the boot if they live in squalor and fail to maintain their gardens, Reform UK has warned.

Nigel Farage’s party has promised a major shake-up of social housing including building more than 50,000 council homes a year.



But Reform chairman Lee Anderson said hard-up Brits expect council house tenants living in accommodation subsidised by the taxpayer to be left in a “reasonable” state.

He said: “People who live in subsidised housing – paid for, subsidised by the hard-working British taxpayer – what is wrong with expecting them to keep their house to a reasonable standard?”



Mr Anderson warned that councils failing to screen tenants properly was “creating mayhem and disturbances on these brand new housing estates.

He added: “The hard-working British taxpayer, the alarm clock people who get up at five or six o’clock in the morning, go to work and they see the house next door with four foot of weeds, dustbin not been emptied for three weeks, and a waft of weed coming out the window – it’s not acceptable.”



His comments come as Reform unveiled its plans to overhaul social housing in Britain.

Young married couples who work and have children would be moved to the front of the queue as well as veterans.

Mr Farage’s party wanted to revive the Right to Buy policy.

This is channelling an old policy put forward by Margaret Thatcher in the 1980s.



Foreign nationals living in social housing will be evicted within a short-time frame as a Reform government takes power.

News.title: Adult film star and influencer Christian Styles dies aged 29 as heartbroken family pay tribute
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

ADULT STAR GONE Adult film star and influencer Christian Styles dies aged 29 as heartbroken family pay tribute

AN ADULT film star and content creator has died aged 29 following a “sudden and heartbreaking” loss as family and friends pay tribute.

Zachary Jaghab, who boasted over a million followers on his Instagram, died on August 20.



Zachary, whose stage name was Christian Styles, has been remembered as “the sweetest man” following his tragic death.

He was a successful influencer and is survived by his parents and two siblings.



Born and raised in Michigan, Zachary first broke into the adult industry in 2021.

Across his social media he has amassed a large following, particularly on X where he promoted his OnlyFans work.



In an online GoFundMe, a representative for the family said: “This unimaginable loss has left a beautiful Canton family grieving the passing of someone deeply loved.

“As they face the pain of losing Zack, Johnny and Ellen are also carrying their own serious health struggles, including cancer, making this season even more overwhelming.”

People have been quick to flock online posting their tributes to the young man.

One person said: “Rest in peace sweet angel. You were and are so loved.”



Another said: “We will miss you terribly.”

A third said: “Rest in peace Christian. May you find lots of joy and happiness in the everafter.”

A final said: “Christian leaves behind much more than images, videos, or memories.

“He leaves a lasting mark on our community and on everyone who connected with him, followed him, and shared part of his story.”

Zachary’s cause of death is not currently known.

News.title: Horror moment mafia boss is shot dead at point-blank range by assassin after his gang was ‘involved in blood feuds’
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment an Israeli mafia don embroiled in “blood feuds” is shot dead at point- blank range.

Arch-criminal Yanis Yushvaev was assassinated as he left a petrol station near Caesarea, a town around 30 miles north of Tel Aviv.



Distressing CCTV footage, which The Sun has chosen not to show in full, sees a gunman wearing a hat, hoodie and glasses casually walk up a short flight of stairs.

Yushvaev, 40, is seen exiting the building flanked by two associates as the assassin pressed up against the glass door.



Moments later, the shooter pulls out a pistol and fires into the back of Yushvaev’s head as the three men have their backs turned.

The crime boss is seen tumbling down the stairs as the gunman flees on foot.

Yushvaev was critically injured and pronounced dead shortly afterwards.

Cops said the killing was criminally motivated and have launched a major manhunt for suspects who they believe fled in a vehicle.



Yushvaev was one of Israel’s most feared gangsters and was repeatedly arrested in connection with shootings, arsons and violent criminal underworld clashes.

Police described him as the leader of an organised crime group associated with Israel’s Caucasus community that was involved in a number of feuds.

A decade ago, Yushvaev was shot and wounded in Hadera, a city just north of Caesarea, but recovered from his injuries and bolstered his influence.



Police accused him of targeting the home of a Hadera businessman and wounding a civilian in shootings last June, but he was released without charge.

Yushvaev’s death comes just six months after he was arrested at Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion airport on his way back from Moscow.

In that case, intelligence suggested that he had returned with the intention of harming rival gang members, Ynet reported.

He was eventually released due to insufficient evidence.

Yushvaev was indicted in 2021 after threatening to murder a businessman if he didn’t pay a $1.1million (£800,000) debt.



The mafia boss was known to demand “complete loyalty” from his henchmen.

He would “almost never” talk on the phone to evade wiretaps, leading to a police source saying it was frustratingly “hard to convict him”.

Yushvaev’s killing comes as Israel grapples with a growing organised crime problem.

Feuds have increasingly spilled into public arenas, with thirteen attacks reported in just a number of days, according to The Telegraph.

Branches of the popular sushi chain Japanika have recently been targeted with grenades, gunfire and arson attacks in what cops have linked to clashes between the Mosli (Jewish) and Jarushi (Arab) crime families.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Murders are reportedly sharply on the rise, with 309 recorded in Israel last year, a 109 per cent increase on the 148 victims in 2022.

National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has been criticised for his inaction and denied accusations that he is treating it as an internal Arab problem.

News.title: Diner left disgusted after waiter leaves note on bill for chef to 'spit in her eggs'
News.content:
Diner left disgusted after waiter leaves note on bill for chef to 'spit in her eggs'

A Brazilian tourist and her family were visiting a restaurant in when she ordered a breakfast of scrambled eggs, juice and coffee - but the bill said it came with an unexpected surprise

View 3 Images The receipt read: "This is pissing me off. Burn the eggs and spit in them." (Image: Azzurro)

A diner was left shocked when her bill arrived at a restaurant and she discovered that the chef had been told to spit in her food.

‌



Maria Clara, a Brazilian tourist, and her family were visiting Victor Lab restaurant in Romagna, Italy on August 19 when she ordered a breakfast of scrambled eggs, juice and coffee.

‌



When her food arrived, she noticed the eggs were runny and asked her server for them to be a "little more cooked".

‌



The server allegedly scoffed that they "don't make raw eggs here".

"In the end, they arrived very soft, but I didn't ask for them to be recooked," she recalled. "I let it go because I didn't want to argue," Clara said.

When her receipt arrived, Clara was shocked at what she found. She included the receipt in a one-star Google review of the establishment.

‌



It read: "This is pissing me off. Burn the eggs and spit in them."

View 3 Images Clara noticed the eggs were runny and asked her server for them to be a "little more cooked" (stock image) (Image: Getty)

This was flagged with the managers and Clara said the 17-year-old server got "very nervous."

‌



He apologized and said it was a joke between him and the chef.

The teen tried to throw the receipt away, but she threatened to call the police if he did.

The restaurant subsequently apologized to Clara under her review, saying: "The behavior you reported was absolutely inappropriate and in no way reflects the values, customer service, and professional standards we strive to ensure every day."

‌



But Victor Lab subsequently uploaded a video to their TikTok account that appeared to mock the incident.

View 3 Images The incident occurred at Victor Lab restaurant (Image: TikTok)

The video depicts the restaurant owner as a demanding customer who orders a dish with "spit."

Article continues below

"Sometimes it almost makes you laugh when you watch it, but this isn't a laughing matter," she said.

"It's serious," said Clara.

She reportedly asked that her last name not be shared as she has received death threats.

News.title: Lidl £10 furniture item looks just like £28 The Range and £42 B&Q available now
News.content:
Lidl £10 furniture item looks just like £28 The Range and £42 B&Q available now

Lidl is selling an item that bears a striking resemblance to more high-end options at The Range and B&Q

People looking for an affordable way to make remote working easier and more comfortable- or to have breakfast in bed without the risk of getting crumbs everywhere - may take a liking to a furniture item on sale at Lidl. The supermarket, which has roughly 1,000 stores dotted throughout the UK, claims the piece is "space-saving".

‌



Lidl is best known for its affordable groceries, but recently it's been getting plenty of attention for its 'Middle of Lidl' aisle. It stocks a rotating selection of homeware deals, seasonal items, DIY tools and garden accessories.

‌



The LIVARNO Bed Tray is the latest expected to get shoppers raving. It retails for £9.99, and has a bamboo look that can be deployed in living spaces and bedrooms.

‌



When not in use, it can be folded up and hidden away without taking up much space. When in use, however, it has four legs that help it stand a more-than-sizeable 23.5cm tall.

View 3 Images The LIVARNO Bed Tray at Lidl (Image: Lidl)

Product features - full list

Made from bamboo

With integrated handles and convenient fold-down legs

Can also be used as a serving tray

Space-saving storage

Size when unfolded: W64 x H23.5 x D30cm

Size when folded : W50 x H6 x D30cm

Max. load: 2kg

‌



Shoppers interested in finding out more are urged to visit the Lidl website. Please note, this is for in-store collection only, home delivery is not an option.

View 3 Images The Bamboo Bed Tray Table at The Range (Image: The Range)

It bears a striking resemblance to more high-end options on the market. Take The Range, for instance, which is stocking the Bamboo Bed Tray Table for £27.99.

‌



The biggest difference between the two - other than the £17 in price - is that it comes as a pack of two. It works out to roughly £14 per tray, which is still more expensive than the Lidl version.

Describing the product, The Range said: "Ideal for serving breakfast and dinner, this breakfast tray also can be used as a writing or drawing table for work on the bed such as reading books, surfing with a laptop, writing log etc. This portable bed tray can be widely used by kids, couples, elders in kitchen, bedroom, bed, sofa and hospital etc.

"Sturdy construction is the inherent advantage of natural bamboo breakfast tray. Made from eco-friendly organic bamboo, the bed trays for breakfast are great alternative to plastic as it is a renewable and sustainable material.

‌



View 3 Images The Bamboo Folding Bed Tray at B&Q (Image: B&Q)

"Foldable legs allow the eating trays to be laid flat and not shaken and save more space when storage. Built-in carrying handles makes transporting food or other surface items with ease."

Meanwhile, there's also the Bamboo Folding Bed Tray at B&Q, which also comes as a pack of two, for £41.99. The product description reads: "Make relaxing at home more comfortable with this 2-in-1 Bamboo Bed Tray Table. Designed for versatility, it works as both a raised lap desk and a flat serving tray.

Article continues below

"The foldable legs collapse smoothly for compact storage, making it ideal for modern homes. Whether you're enjoying breakfast in bed, working on your laptop, serving guests, or relaxing on the sofa, this sturdy yet lightweight bamboo tray delivers style, convenience, and practicality in one elegant design."

News.title: Heartbreaking reason boys used mum's perfume – two weeks before dad killed them
News.content:
Heartbreaking reason boys used mum's perfume – two weeks before dad killed them

WARNING, DISTRESSING CONTENT: Claire Throssell tragically lost both of her children almost 12 years ago and she has now recalled how she caught them using her perfume two weeks before their murder

View 5 Images Claire Throsell with her boys Paul (left) and Jack (right) (Image: Supplied)

A mum whose precious sons were burnt to death by their abusive dad has revealed the heartbreaking reason the boys doused themselves in her perfume two weeks before being murdered.

‌



Claire Throssell lost her children, Jack, 12, and Paul, nine, when their father, Darren Sykes, lured them to the attic by pretending there was a new train set there. He then barricaded them inside and set fire to the family home.

‌



Evil Sykes also died in the blaze, with the horrifying incident happening during a court-approved access visit in October 2014. Claire, from Penistone, South Yorkshire, had warned Cafcass (Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service) and Social Services that she believed her ex-husband was capable of killing Jack and Paul.

‌



She said he had been violent and abusive to both her and the boys — which is a reason for why she separated from him. However, after Sykes filed for custody and brought the matter to the courts, he was awarded five hours of unsupervised access to the boys every week.

Then, on October 22, 2014, during one of the visits, Claire’s worst nightmare became a reality. And now, speaking on the Tom’s Talks Podcast, she revealed how she caught her sons dousing themselves in her perfume just two weeks before their brutal murders, and the reason why is deeply upsetting.

View 5 Images Claire shared an extremely close bond with her two sons (Image: MDM)

‌



She said: “Just two weeks before what happened, happened, I caught them spraying themselves with my perfume and I had to bite my lip because my perfume’s expensive and I thought, ‘My bottle’s going down and I’m not wearing it. What is happening?’”

She spotted Jack and Paul spraying themselves with it after going upstairs.

The devastated mum remembered: “I had to bite my lip obviously and went, ‘Boys, what are you doing with my perfume? If you want aftershave, I’ll buy you aftershave.’

‌



View 5 Images Darren Sykes, 44, killed his children in a house fire (Image: MDM)

“And they went, ‘It’s not that, we are scared of dad and we are taking you with us. We want a part of you with us wherever you go. Where you are mum is home.’”

After a pause to gather her emotions, she added: “The only safety plan the police could come up with was buying them a mobile phone and if they felt scared, text me and I could go fetch them. They were nine and 12 years old…”

‌



Sykes lit 14 different fires using petrol before barricading the house shut. Speaking to the Mirror last year, Claire said: “The last words Jack said, as the firefighters desperately tried to rescue him, was, ‘My dad did this and he did it on purpose’.”

View 5 Images Paul and Jack Throssell (Image: DAILY MIRROR)

Paul died that night while Jack clung to life for the next five days before severe burns and medical complications brought his suffering to a close.

‌



Since then, Claire has campaigned for family law to change, and last October, the government announced plans to repeal the presumption that kids should have contact with both parents in relation to family court decisions.

Claire’s determination to see change has meant family courts are safer — and it is now mandatory for courts to establish whether children are at risk of harm from a contact order.

View 5 Images Paul (left) and Jack (right) (Image: Supplied)

Article continues below

Claire, who is now an ambassador for Women’s Aid and IDAS (Independent Domestic Abuse Service), also published a book in October called For My Boys.

And speaking to us last year, she said: “I will not let Jack and Paul’s deaths be in vain. There isn’t a single minute of a single day when I don’t think about my sons. Jack should now be 23 and Paul 20.

“Their lives were cruelly taken far too early, and I was robbed of the memories and lives we should have shared together.”

News.title: Suspect 'found dead in car' after bodies of five people discovered by police in Oregon
News.content:
Suspect 'found dead in car' after bodies of five people discovered by police in Oregon

Police have not said how five people were killed as a homicide investigation has found the prime suspect dead in his car more than 180 miles away

View 3 Images Five people and 'several' pets were found dead on a rural Oregon property in a horrific scene authorities are now investigating as a quintuple homicide (Image: KPTV)

Mystery surrounds the deaths of five people after police discovered the body of the prime suspect more than 180 miles away.

‌



Police tragically confirmed the discovery of five bodies at an address in Forest Grove, a town 30 miles west of Portland, the largest city in Oregon, on Saturday (August 22). Emergency services had been called to a vehicle fire.

‌



A manhunt was launched to find the suspect f or the homicides. On Tuesday (August 25), they announced they located 36-year-old Benjamin Charles Parker dead in his car in Enumclaw, Washington, 187 miles north of the address.

‌



They also confirmed the identities of the people killed. However, mystery still surrounds exactly how they died.

The Washington County Sheriff’s Office said the victims include Parker’s girlfriend, 26-year-old Stella Jade Kimsey; her 60-year-old mother, Rowan Karla Kimsey; and her 85-year-old grandmother, Mary Elizabeth Kimsey.

View 3 Images A police command centre leaving the scene in Oregon (Image: Mark Graves/The Oregonian via AP)

‌



Stella Kimsey’s best friend, 26-year-old Linsey Mae Haraldsen, and Haraldsen’s partner, Alvin Raymond Chu, 27, were also among the dead. Authorities said Rowan Kimsey owned the property about 30 miles west of Portland and lived there with her daughter, Stella, along with Parker.

Two cats and two dogs were also found dead at the scene. Another cat was transported to a vet for treatment but was later euthanized due to the extent of its injuries. The sheriff’s office did not specify how the people and animals died in a new update issued on Tuesday.

View 3 Images Sheriff Caprice Massey speaking to reporters (Image: FOX12)

‌



Authorities found the five bodies on Saturday and announced the homicide investigation on Sunday. They noted the complexity of the investigation and the large crime scene.

“I will say that in my 22 years here, I have not been a part of or witnessed a scene quite this complex involving this type of an investigation,” Sheriff Caprice Massey said.

Article continues below

In an initial press conference held on Monday, Sheriff Massey also urged anyone who is familiar with the property or the people who live there to share any information they may have.

News.title: 'Multiple children and adults' dead after US shooting and house fire
News.content:
'Multiple children and adults' dead after US shooting and house fire

Police are carrying out a 'very complex' investigation after multiple people, including children, were killed in a fire and shooting in Montana in the United States

View 3 Images Huge flames engulfed the entire property (Image: Dave Hiller/ KTVQ News)

Multiple people, including children, have died after a shooting and fire at a home in the US.

‌



The family members died at a Billings West End home on Sunday after police rushed to the scene following reports of a fire.

‌



In the initial 911 call to the residence at 315 White Star Circle, gunshots could be heard in the background.

‌



View 3 Images The entire home was engulfed by flames (Image: X)

Montana police announced on Monday that children and adults were killed in the incident and the male suspect is dead.

Interim Yellowstone County Sheriff Kent O’Donnell said at a news conference that law enforcement has identified all people involved in the incident, including a suspect, but is not yet releasing their names.

‌



O’Donnell said that the incident began as a family disturbance, and he was “deeply saddened” after speaking with family members of those involved.

He said: “As you can see, just by the amount of agencies involved in this, this is a very, very complex investigation.

"When the call went out last night for assistance, the cavalry was coming.”

‌



Billings Fire Chief Matt Hoppel when firefighters arrived at the scene at 6.02pm they encountered gunfire, preventing them from conducting normal suppression efforts.

The scene became complex and dangerous and emergency services worked to secure the area and keep the public safe.

View 3 Images The number or identities of those dead has yet to be confirmed (Image: X)

‌



Hoppel said: "Because the scene could not be immediately confirmed as secure, our firefighters were unable to operate as we normally would."

Firefighters had to tackle the flames using water from trucks due to the lack of fire hydrants in the area, slowing down the response.

Fire crews were able to ensure the blaze did not spread to any other properties.

‌



Officials confirmed that the house was fully consumed by the flames with neighbouring homes sustaining minor heat damage.

Billings Assistant Police Chief Shawn Mayo said a man was discovered outside the home with a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

He was taken to a hospital and later died.

Article continues below

O’Donnell said deputies from Stillwater and Carbon counties also responded to assist.

The cause of the fire is yet to be determined and the investigation continues, with O'Donnell claiming more information will be released on Wednesday.

News.title: UK drone factories could be attacked by 'unknown sources' Kremlin adviser warns
News.content:
UK drone factories could be attacked by 'unknown sources' Kremlin adviser warns

Former Russian deputy foreign minister Andrei Fedorov said he could not "100% exclude" the prospect of "semi-military" action against the UK as tensions escalate over British support for Ukraine

View 5 Images Tensions escalate over British support for Ukraine (Image: Getty)

A Kremlin adviser has warned that UK factories manufacturing drones for Ukraine could face attacks from "unknown sources" after Britain agreed to share long-range missile blueprints with the war-ravaged nation.

‌



Former Russian deputy foreign minister Andrei Fedorov said he could not "100% exclude" the possibility of "semi-military" action against Britain, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham made his first overseas visit to Kyiv since taking office at No 10.

‌



During the trip, the UK reaffirmed its "unwavering" support for Ukraine, which in turn handed over what officials have described as a "goldmine" of battlefield data to help strengthen British security.

‌



View 5 Images During his visit, the Prime Minister pressed Ukraine's allies to dispatch more interceptor missiles to Kyiv (Image: Getty Images)

Mr Fedorov warned that "sooner or later, there might be not only verbal but maybe some visible reaction from Russia towards the UK".

When pressed on what form this might take, he said: "There are different discussions how it should look like – it might be so-called technical reaction, maybe some hackers attack from unknown source, not from official level of course.

‌



"There might be different political steps and I cannot exclude 100% that there might be some semi-military, for example."

When pushed further to clarify what he meant by "semi-military", he told BBC Newsnight: "For example, something might happen with enterprises, with the factories which are producing drones for Ukraine, etc etc."

View 5 Images Andy Burnham reacts as he is shown the rubbles and wreckages left on the buildings and site of a strike by the Lukanivska market, in Kyiv (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



When asked whether this meant British factories on home soil could face military strikes from Russia, the adviser responded: "They could be attacked, not by Russia, but by... from unknown sources."

The UK has agreed to declassify blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French-produced version of the Storm Shadow that has already been deployed to strike targets inside Russia.

The move has drawn fierce condemnation from Moscow, with President Vladimir Putin's spokesman Dmitry Peskov warning it would add "fuel to the fire" of the ongoing conflict.

‌



However, Mr Burnham hit back at reporters in Kyiv: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?".

During his visit, the Prime Minister pressed Ukraine's allies to dispatch more interceptor missiles to Kyiv as the country continues to struggle under relentless Russian bombardment.

He co-chaired his first coalition of the willing meeting, declaring that the group was doing "everything we can" to "dig into our own stocks and help others dig into their stocks".

‌



View 5 Images Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly pleaded for more US-made Patriot interceptor missiles (Image: STRINGER/EPA/Shutterstock)

Stocks of Patriots have been redirected to the Middle East following the outbreak of war with Iran, leaving Ukraine receiving significantly fewer missiles this year compared to previous years. Russia has sought to exploit the shortage by intensifying its ballistic missile strikes, killing at least 23 people and wounding more than 100 in just the past three days.

Speaking later on Monday, Mr Zelensky welcomed the talks between the coalition of the willing but warned that "now, we have to deal with a funding gap", raising the possibility of bringing forward part of the European loan to Ukraine, or unlocking frozen Russian assets.

‌



"The total gap is 27 billion," he said in a post on X.

"One of the main options is to bring forward part of the European loan funding this year. But we should not give up on other ideas for how to ensure fair protection in this war – a war that Russia started and continues to prolong."

"Obviously, with a change of prime minister, presumably people might think is there a change of policy – well, I'm here to say there isn't," he told ITV News.

‌



Mr Burnham and Mr Zelensky have also signed an agreement granting the Ministry of Defence, working alongside selected British firms, access to Ukraine's "Avengers" AI database, Downing Street confirmed.

View 5 Images The Prime Minister also pledged "continuity" in Britain's approach to Ukraine, insisting "we're not a fair-weather friend, we're here for the long haul". (Image: Henry Nicholls/PA Wire)

The deal is anticipated to help the UK draw on Ukraine's frontline experience and develop AI-driven solutions to national security challenges facing both nations. While the agreement is initially centred on defence and security, officials suggest the deal could "revolutionise all parts of public life, from air traffic control to train systems".

Article continues below

The first trial of the new partnership is expected to see AI sensors provide an additional layer of protection for military bases, guarding against protestors and hostile actors. A second project will see the UK and Ukraine join forces on low-power AI chips that could power a new generation of longer-lasting machines capable of operating in more hostile environments.

No 10 described the so-called "Avengers AI Labs" as "a goldmine of battlefield data" which would afford British researchers "unparalleled access to real-world operational insights and the opportunity to 'plug and play'."

News.title: EasyJet starts drive to recruit new wave of over 50s cabin crew
News.content:
EasyJet starts drive to recruit new wave of over 50s cabin crew

EasyJet says the number of cabin crew over the age of 50 has more than doubled - with over-60s almost quadrupling - and so it has extended a new recruitment push

View 2 Images Easyjet cabin crew members smile for a snap at Gatwick Airport (Image: David Parry/PA Media Assignments)

Budget airline easyJet is launching a new recruitment drive to hire more older workers as cabin crew.

‌



The no-frills carrier says it follows the success of a previous initiative in 2022, with the number of cabin crew over the age of 50 more than doubling to over 600, and over-60s almost quadrupling.

‌



With a new recruitment push for hundreds of new crew roles for 2027 set to open next month, the airline wants to encourage even more to join.

‌



Among those to take the plunge was Francesca Hicks, 64, a former secretary and nurse for those living with dementia. She attended a taster open day, submitted her formal application, and completed a series of interviews before joining her easyJet cabin crew training course. Eighteen months on, she is now a fully trained cabin crew member and has taken to the skies over 250 times.

View 2 Images Easyjet says passengers appreciate different ages represented among cabin crew on board (Image: Getty)

EasyJet customers urged to check if they are entitled to £500 flight compensation READ MORE :

Francesca said: “When the opportunity to join easyJet as cabin crew came up, I jumped at the chance. I knew I already held all the skills required for the job, but it gave me another way to use my communication, organisation and interpersonal skills in a new and exciting setting.

‌



“The reception both I and my fellow new joiners have received has been overwhelmingly positive. This, and the experiences I’ve had over the past 18 months, have given me a confidence and sense of fulfilment that I’ll take with me through the next stage of my career.”

EasyJet says the new wave of older workers has brought years of experience, and signficant enthusiasm.

It added that many people assume cabin crew is a job for younger workers, and worried they would be the oldest in the team.

‌



Michael Brown, its director of cabin services at easyJet, said: “We want more over-50s to apply as they not only bring their existing skills to excel in a career at easyJet, but also a wealth of life experience that is appreciated by our customers and colleagues alike, which is at the heart of the fantastic service our crew are known for.”

Employment minister Andrew Western said: “Supportive employers like easyJet know the breadth of experience over-50s can bring to the workforce and it shows what can be achieved when this is valued.”

EasyJet says the increase in more over 50s had also brought a strong “culture of mentorship” amongst easyJet’s crew. Over half of its older workers surveyed said they feel like a mentor to younger colleagues.

Article continues below

Nearly seven in 10 crew say that travellers of all ages are happy to see different generations represented on board.

Applications open from September, with opportunities available across the airline’s UK bases.

News.title: Some high street coffee - including Costa's cappuccino - packed with same caffeine as FOUR cans of Red Bull
News.content:
Some high street coffee - including Costa's cappuccino - packed with same caffeine as FOUR cans of Red Bull

Tests by consumer group Which? have discovered large variations in the amount of caffeine in drinks sold by big name coffee chains, including Caffè Nero and Starbucks

View 4 Images Costa Coffee found to have some of the highest caffeine contents in analysis by Which? (Image: Getty Images)

Some chain store coffee can contain almost as much caffeine as four cans of Red Bull, research has revealed.

‌



Consumer group Which? examined the caffeine content of an espresso, cappuccino, filter coffee, latte, americano, flat white and matcha at high street giants Caffè Nero, Costa, Greggs, Pret a Manger and Starbucks. Not every chain offers all seven products, and they often vary in size of serving.

‌



It found those looking for a morning pick-me-up could be getting a much bigger caffeine hit at some than others.

‌



Costa had the strongest medium cappuccino, at 325mg of caffeine per cup. That is around the same amount as four cans of energy drink Red Bull (80mg per can), and nearly three and a half times as much as a Starbucks cappuccino, which has 89mg.

One reason Costa's cappuccino packs such a punch is that it contains up to four espresso shots, according to Which?

View 4 Images Which? found that Costa offers the strongest medium cappuccino (Image: whitemay via Getty Images)

‌



The second and third highest cappuccino caffeine levels, Greggs and Caffè Nero, were significantly below Costa at 235mg and 221mg respectively.

Caffeine is a natural stimulant that affects the brain and nervous system. It makes people more alert, increases attention and has been shown to increase performance in short-term high-intensity and endurance exercise.

However, while those after an energy surge might lean towards the stronger options identified by Which?, people sensitive to caffeine or those advised to restrict their intake for health reasons, including pregnancy, should be cautious and steer clear of the most powerful brews.

‌



The British Heart Foundation advises that up to 400 mg of caffeine a day is safe and not linked to bad health effects. The exact limit depends on your body size, how fast you process caffeine, and your overall health. And the NHS Pregnancy Advice recommends pregnant women limit caffeine intake to a maximum of 200mg per day.

Those after the most bang for their buck from an espresso get 180mg of caffeine in a 50ml shot at Pret, 100mg in a 30ml serving at Costa, 75mg at Greggs, 67mg at Caffe Nero, to a low of 45mg in a 24ml shot at Starbucks.

View 4 Images Pret a Manger hads the strongest espresso in tests by Which? (Image: Brian Dillon)

‌



US heavyweight Starbucks also had the weakest latte for caffeine, according to Which?, at 89mg in a 354ml serving. That compared to 200mg at Costa, 208mg in a slightly larger sized serving at Greggs, 175mg at Caffe Nero, and 180mg at Pret.

Which? pointed out that the type of coffee bean used for firms can make a big difference. Robusta beans contain roughly double the caffeine content of Arabica beans.

View 4 Images Starbucks had the lowest caffeine content for an espresso and latte, Which? found, although that might be better for certain drinkers

‌



The research also found that americanos had the widest caffeine spread across chains. A standard medium size ranges from a gentle 89 mg at Starbucks all the way to a potent 325 mg at Costa Coffee.

Jessica Carson, Which? health and wellbeing expert, said: “For many of us, there is nothing quite like a strong cup of coffee to start the day.

“Our research shows caffeine content varies wildly from chain to chain. If you drink multiple cups a day or need to cut back for health reasons, pay attention to where you shop and what you order to avoid any unwanted side effects.”

Article continues below

A Costa Coffee spokesperson said: "At Costa Coffee, we're committed to helping customers make informed choices. That's why caffeine and nutritional information is available across our menu and online, so customers can choose the drinks that best suit their individual preferences and needs. We also offer decaffeinated coffee and a range of non-caffeinated drinks. Coffee naturally contains caffeine and levels can vary depending on factors such as the blend, recipe and serving size."

News.title: More than 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England over 10 years
News.content:
The 22-year-old spent the final months of her pregnancy and the first weeks of her son's life living in a hotel.

She says she has no idea how long she will be expected to stay there but was told it would only be temporary.

"I'm just scared when he gets older, when he starts crawling around, I can't even allow him to crawl in such a place like that because it's so dirty," she says.

While pregnant, Natasha says her room became infested with ants, which she repeatedly reported before eventually being moved into another room.

But her problems didn't end there.

While Natasha has her own bathroom, she shares a kitchen with around 60 other residents. She says the hotel is home to a mix of people, not just mothers and babies, and that she does not always feel safe using the shared space with Zayd.

Natasha describes living there as feeling "like a prison". She says visitors are not allowed, meaning friends and family can not come to help her with her five-week-old boy.

"I just want somewhere peaceful for him and calm. Somewhere nice where I can bring him up," she says.

She is one of the 1.34 million households on social housing waiting lists as of March 2025, the latest government figures.

London will see the largest share of funding, although no figure has been given for how many homes will be built in the capital.

Ministers said Monday's allocation was the first stage of the 10-year programme and more than Â£16bn remains to be allocated outside London.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner suggested some of the new homes will be built by councils, saying she and the prime minister were "doing everything we can to get councils building once again".

Burnham had previously promised "the biggest council house building programme since the post-war period", and the government said millions extra would be given to councils to support their housebuilding plans and help with expertise.

But the announcement stops short of clarifying how the funding will be split between council homes and those provided by housing associations.

News.title: Beyond China's humanoid robots, a quieter machine revolution is unfolding
News.content:
"I take a nap and the world changes," says Chen Tianyu.

His world certainly does. The 28-year-old keeps up with the latest technology by spending his spare time in factories that are switching to automation. That way he knows what to prioritise when teaching his class about artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics.

In front of him, around 30 college students are studying code. One of them is typing furiously as his eyes dart from the screen to the robot: "The idea is it will grab that cylindrical piece and move it over there."

A line of industrial robots are waiting to be programmed, and in another part of the classroom, students are trying to develop robotic medical instruments. As he guides them, Chen declares: "If you are not needed by the world of AI and robotics, then you'll definitely be among those eliminated".

For the people in this room, this is a step - or rather a leap - towards a future that China is meticulously building: Xi Jinping's $20bn (Â£14.7bn) plan to put his country at the forefront of innovation and in direct competition with the US.

The evidence is all around them. They are in the Hangzhou Technician Institute, one of several huge, purpose-built vocational schools that want to churn out the next generation of tech-savvy engineers. The campus sits on the outskirts of Hangzhou, a former imperial capital whose futuristic skyline is just the first hint of its role as a global tech hub.

Across the country, there are more than two million robots working in China's factories - which is more than anywhere else - and they are continuing to scale up at extraordinary speed.

News.title: The grieving family who say the coroner's courts aren't working
News.content:
Sarah thought she knew what she was getting into when she attended a coroner's court in May 2024 to discuss the death of her second cousin.

Her day job as a murder detective meant she was used to courts, to judges, to legal argument. What she wasn't prepared for was a coroner's court. "I felt like I was on trial," she recalls of her first hearing, in Woking, Surrey. "I remember just feeling completely railroadedâ¦ It [was] far more hostile than I had ever expected."

Her cousin, Daniel Lindsay, died in 2023, aged 41. He had lived at a home in Surrey that specialises in caring for people with learning disabilities. Daniel also had Down Syndrome and type 1 diabetes.

As his death was unexpected, his case was referred to the coroner for an inquest.

What followed was one of the most stressful experiences of Sarah's life. She discovered new details about how her cousin lived, and his cause of death. The family initially thought Daniel died from a heart attack - but over the inquest, they learnt that was wrong. She had expected the process to be emotional; what she didn't predict was just how complex and frustrating it would be, at times leaving her tearful and furious.

Coroners examine deaths that are not straightforward, like unexpected or violent deaths, or those that take place in state custody. Every year, thousands of British families rely on these courts for crucial answers. For many, an inquest provides the key interaction with the arms of the state at a time of trauma.

News.title: Organised crime arrests as police investigate A66 crash that killed two officers
News.content:
Twelve people have been arrested as part of the investigation into the A66 crash that killed seven people, including two police officers.

Nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, have been arrested across Teesside on suspicion of a range of offences including possession of a firearm and being part of an organised crime group. One has since been charged.

In the early hours of Saturday, a Volkswagen Passat that had been pursued by police travelled the wrong way down the A66 near Middlesbrough and crashed into an oncoming police car - two PCs and all five Passat occupants died.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating "serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident".

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and 17-year-old Cole Robert Worthy.

Earlier, Cleveland Police released more details of its investigation into the lead-up to the crash and information about the 12 people it had arrested.

The force said:

It received several reports of two vehicles "being driven dangerously" on Saturday morning

The first vehicle, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was seen "ramming properties" in the Middlesbrough area

The second vehicle, a Passat, is believed to have been associated with this activity

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology

The Volvo has been recovered in Middlesbrough

Four of the five people in the Passat had previous convictions

Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said the investigation had been "fast moving and complex".

He said: "The events of that tragic night will have a lasting and profound impact on the Cleveland area and the communities we seek to protect.

"We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident and to bring all those responsible to justice."

News.title: HPV home-testing kits available for women in England who have missed cervical screening
News.content:
Dr Sue Mann, national clinical director for women's health, said: "Offering millions of women an alternative test they can do from the comfort of their own homes will be a game-changer â making it easier than ever for them to get tested.

"There are lots of reasons that may stop women from getting their cervical screening â embarrassment, lack of time or worries about discomfort â and these kits provide a discreet and convenient option we hope will encourage more women to take up the life-saving test."

The kits contain a swab, similar to a long cotton, bud which is used to collect a sample from the vagina.

It is then sent back to the NHS and if high-risk HPV is found, individuals will be invited to book a follow-up cervical screening appointment.

High-risk HPV increases the risk of cervical cancer, but it does not mean a woman will automatically develop it.

Trials of the self-testing in London suggest it could lead to one in 10 women to come forward for screening â boosting uptake by around 400,000 a year.

Other parts of the UK are also looking at introducing self-testing.

Women aged 24 to 64 are invited for cervical screening every five years â or more frequently if HPV is detected.

Through a combination of HPV vaccination, which is offered to teenagers, and improved screening, the NHS is hoping to eliminate cervical cancer by 2040.

The NHS says cervical screening appointments with a clinician is still the best way to prevent cancer â and even if you have missed an appointment you can still come forward for one.

News.title: Sir Chris Hoy: Campaigning for cancer screening should not be down to me
News.content:
Sir Chris Hoy believes the onus to encourage men to get tested for prostate cancer should not just be on high-profile individuals like him.

Hoy told BBC Scotland he felt privileged to have the public platform to spread awareness and would continue to do so even if there was a national screening system in place.

But he said: "It shouldn't just be down to high-profile individuals like Jeremy Clarkson or myself or any number of men who've been in a similar situation.

"There should be a more systematic and proactive approach to let men know about their own risk."

Sir Chris was diagnosed with stage 4 prostate cancer when was 47. He turned 50 in March.

News.title: Asbestos killed my mum in her 40s – was her school to blame?
News.content:
When Caroline Bryan was enjoying high school with friends in the early 90s, she would never have imagined replaying those memories in her final weeks, while searching for answers about her terminal condition.

The mum was 46 when she died from mesothelioma, an incurable cancer linked to asbestos exposure.

As she came to terms with her difficult diagnosis, Caroline's belief was the only place she could have encountered asbestos was during her time at school decades earlier.

Her family blame the local authority that ran Caroline's school for her death and are taking legal action. Cardiff council said it would be inappropriate to comment on ongoing legal proceedings.

"She never had the sort of career that would have exposed her to asbestos," said Caroline's daughter Brooklyn.

"We never lived in any houses that would have had asbestos in."

Caroline was mostly a stay at home mum and the family hadn't heard of mesothelioma before, but quickly learned it likely came from asbestos fibres she will have unknowingly breathed in many years before.

News.title: Videos showing dangerous driving easily found on social media
News.content:
At least one of the young people killed in the Middlesbrough crash appears in multiple videos posted on TikTok depicting dangerous driving.

BBC Verify has found dozens of videos on social media showing high-speed car chases, driving on footpaths and on the wrong side of the road.

TikTok's policies prohibit content that "could lead to physical harm", and the company has removed videos identified by BBC Verify.

Cleveland Police say they are launching a wide-scale investigation "into the criminality which took place prior to the fatal crash", and "there is no evidence to indicate that filming of the activities that took place on Friday night and Saturday morning has taken place for the purposes of TikTok".

Merlyn Thomas reports.

Video produced by Tom Joyner. Graphics by Sally Nicholls and Mesut Ersoz.

News.title: Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
News.content:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine, Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at Â£2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July, despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

News.title: Boy,16, arrested after four viable devices found in security alert
News.content:
A 16-year-old boy has been arrested under the Terrorism Act after a security alert in Omagh, County Tyrone.

Police carried out a planned search on Monday at an address in the Gardenville Avenue.

Police said four viable explosive devices were found and removed from the property for forensic examination.

Nearby residents who had been asked to leave their homes during the alert have since returned.

Det Insp Winters urged the public not to speculate about the incident.

"It's important to stress that, while the suspect has been arrested under the Terrorism Act, our investigation to establish a motive remains very much ongoing."

News.title: Briton fighting for Russia killed in Ukraine
News.content:
A British national has been killed in Ukraine while fighting for Russia.

Bradley Townsend is said to have died following an attack by a remote-controlled FPV drone in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. His death, on 10 June, is believed to be the first of a British citizen fighting for Russia in the conflict.

The 33-year-old left his home in Barnsley, South Yorkshire, earlier this year after telling his family he was going to Romania, according to the Yorkshire Post, external.

The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) confirmed it was aware of reports a British national had died in Ukraine, adding it was in contact with his family.

The news emerged as Andy Burnham arrived in Kyiv for his first foreign trip as UK prime minister.

The visit coincides with the 35th anniversary of the country's independence from the Soviet Union.

The government has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile - allowing Ukraine to produce the weapon domestically.

News.title: Man charged with murder after house fire
News.content:
A man has been charged with murder, attempted murder and arson following a fire in west London that left a woman dead and eight others in need of hospital treatment.

Pawel Kulpa, 34, faces one count of murder, eight counts of attempted murder and one count of arson with intent to endanger life.

The charges come after a fire at a residential address on Berkeley Avenue, Hounslow, at about 01:15 BST on Wednesday, 19 August.

A 48-year-old woman died in hospital while another woman, 40, remains in hospital in a life-threatening condition. Kulpa is due to appear at Willesden Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

News.title: Prince Harry steps down from African wildlife charity board
News.content:
The Duke of Sussex has stepped down from the board of an African wildlife charity whose rangers had been found to have committed human rights abuses against indigenous people.

A spokesman for Prince Harry confirmed he was stepping down after being president for the charity, African Parks, for six years before becoming a member of its board of directors in 2023, but said he remains a "supporter of its mission".

Last year the organisation admitted human rights abuses were committed by its rangers in Congo-Brazzaville.

Prince Harry's resignation comes shortly after it was announced he was relocating with the Duchess of Sussex, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet from California to the UK.

Prince Harry's spokesman said "the Duke is proud of his 10 years with African Parks and fully supports the ongoing strengthening of its board.

"His commitment to conservation in Africa continues, and he remains a supporter of African Parks' mission."

African Parks manages around 20 national parks and protected areas across 12 countries.

It was subject to an independent human rights investigation into allegations guards managed and paid by the charity had beaten, raped and tortured indigenous people in the Odzala-Kokoua National Park.

The charity said in 2025 it had improved its safeguarding processes both in the Odzala-Kokoua National Park and institutionally.

Announcing a "governance refresh of its board of directors", the charity thanked Prince Harry for his association, saying he had "brought global attention to the urgent need for biodiversity protection for the benefit of people and wildlife, and has contributed greatly to promoting philanthropy for the cause of conservation in Africa".

It added: "The duke remains deeply committed to this cause, and remains a strong supporter of African Parks' work."

The charity's website says Prince Harry served as part of the expert team that helped implement the first phase of the 500 Elephants project, which was "one of the largest and most significant elephant translocations in conservation history".

It saw wildlife experts move elephants from a park in Malawi to help increase population in areas where they have been heavily poached.

Prince Harry has said helping move elephants to safer homes was an "amazing" experience.

The Sussexes are back in the spotlight after the revelation last week they were returning to the UK this month after enrolling their children to start at a British school in September.

No change is expected to the official status of Prince Harry and Meghan and they will remain as private individuals.

Their pending return to the UK has raised questions on their security arrangements.

Last year, Prince Harry lost a legal challenge over the levels of security he and his family are entitled to while in the UK.

It is unclear what provisions will be made for their security once they return to the UK.

The couple's plans while they are in the UK are also unclear.

The BBC learned the Duchess of Sussex was in talks to return to acting with a role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, which would be her first significant acting role since her marriage to Prince Harry.

In early 2020, the Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties before settling in California in March that year.

News.title: Snooker champion Graeme Dott guilty of child sex abuse
News.content:
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been found guilty of child sexual abuse.

The 49-year-old denied two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010.

During a trial, the High Court in Glasgow heard that Dott had exposed himself and inappropriately touched a primary school girl in the 1990s and attacked a young boy between 2006 and 2010.

Lord Harrower told Dott, who won the World Snooker Championship in 2006, he would be sentenced at a separate hearing in Edinburgh on 29 September.

Dott, from Glasgow, covered his face with his hands and shook his head while the verdict was delivered by jurors following a five-day trial.

He previously called the allegations made against him "disgusting".

News.title: Drugs dug up at Creamfields site ahead of festival
News.content:
Huge stashes of illegal drugs have been found buried underground at a festival site days before the event was due to begin.

More than 80,000 music fans will head to Creamfields Festival in Daresbury, Cheshire, from Thursday.

About 204 canisters of nitrous oxide - known as laughing gas - and large bags containing ecstasy, MDMA and ketamine tablets were dug up by police during a pre-event search of the grounds, Cheshire Police said.

Supt Andy Blizard said: "Every year, we counter a number of brazen individuals who think they can outsmart us by concealing drugs from view or burying them at the site months in advance."

"There is a zero-tolerance policy regarding drugs," he said.

News.title: Man charged with manslaughter in burglary case
News.content:
A man has been charged with manslaughter after a 75-year-old woman died following a suspected burglary in north London.

Police were called to Tollington Park in Finsbury Park on the night of 11 August after reports of a burglary.

Rose Smith was taken to hospital, where she died the following day. An 81-year-old man was also taken to hospital and was discharged the next day.

Jeffrey Dean Rose, 46, of Apsley Close, North Harrow, has been charged with manslaughter and aggravated burglary. He is due to appear at Barkingside Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

He was arrested on Friday, 21 August.

In a statement released earlier on Monday, Smith's family described her as an "outgoing woman" who loved "bingo, going to cafÃ©s with her friends and, above all, spending time with her family".

They described their loss as devastating, adding: "She was the life and soul of every party. She had a wonderful personality, a big heart and a way of bringing laughter and happiness wherever she went.

"We want people to remember Rose for the person she truly was - loving, fun, kind, sociable and full of life."

The rape and murder of a three-year-old girl has sparked outrage across Nepal, with demands growing for a swift investigation and tougher laws.

The child went missing from her home in Bara, almost 127km from the capital Kathmandu in Madhesh province, on 16 August. Her mutilated and decomposed body was found at a nearby abandoned house three days later after neighbours reported a smell.

Police said a 24-year-old driver and a 17-year-old helper on a bus were among the suspects arrested in connection with the case.

Bara police spokesperson Min Bahadur Ghale confirmed the girl had been raped and murdered and that suspects had been identified and arrested.

But anger has mounted over the police’s response, including alleged delay in the search for the girl and the release on social media of a video purportedly showing the 17-year-old suspect giving a statement.

The girl’s family alleged that the police didn’t respond with urgency while her father and neighbours mounted a frantic search.

The father alleged that police instead lashed out at them and asked them to name suspects.

“I raised the matter with the police,” he said, according to the Kathmandu Post. “But they said they could not proceed merely on what I was saying, and asked me to file a formal complaint by naming suspects.”

The father also informed police that a local man had disappeared and provided his contact details, the paper reported, but they did not act promptly on the information.

Police have rejected the allegation that they failed to conduct a timely search but have launched an inquiry into the leak of footage purportedly showing the teenage suspect describing the incident to investigators. Police said the leak should not have happened while the investigation was ongoing.

Protests erupted following the recovery of the child’s body last week and continued for several days, with angry locals blocking highways.

Many protesters displayed placards and shouted slogans demanding accountability from police and the government. Demonstrators and activists called for changes to laws related to rape and sexual violence and demanded severe punishment for the perpetrators.

The girl’s body was collected from a local hospital on Sunday and cremated.

The girl’s family secured a written agreement from the government promising to create a memorial in her honour, remove two police officers from operational duties and make laws for such offences stricter.

On Thursday, members of the National Assembly urged the government to strengthen laws to prevent violence against children and women.

According to police records, Nepal saw over 25,000 cases of rape and sexual abuse between 2017 and 2015. At least 3,200 of the victims were under the age of 10.
