Xabi Alonso came to Craven Cottage hoping for another Premier League first. Twenty-two years earlier, he bagged his first English top-flight goal for Liverpool. Against a former Reds team-mate striving for the same goal in Alvaro Arbeloa, he made another happy memory on his managerial bow.

Most pictured his return to England to come with Liverpool; Chelsea fans already seem grateful he’s landed in London. While far from the perfect performance, victory in a five-goal thriller against Fulham brought a lot of encouragement.

A mixture of big spending and summer snubs seems to have forged one of the most dangerous attacking front threes in the league. Morgan Rogers showed signs he was worthy of his £117m price tag. Cole Palmer, with a point to prove after his World Cup omission, suddenly looked like a real problem again after what was, by his standards, a dud of a season. His link-up with Joao Pedro took effect within 31 seconds.

open image in gallery Chelsea’s front three stole the show against Fulham ( Reuters )

“They are going to be a very important part of the team,” recognised Alonso, who now wants the trio’s team-mates to reach the level they exhibited on Monday night. “To build [the team] around them, no. To build the team with them. They need to take responsibility, they need to lead the rest, they need to inspire the rest, because if they do great, the other ones will follow.

“We need to reach them in the best possible situations. We need to have good links to reach them, and they need to help the team to be solid. I'm happy for the three of them. They have played for the team and they have scored, so it's always important for the strikers.”

Some Chelsea players are closer to said level than others. Maxence Lacroix was another debutant to impress; his unlikely assist for Rogers was the icing on the cake of a commanding performance in an otherwise imperfect back three. Jorrel Hato was also influential at left wing-back, his attacking impetus showing just how versatile the defender can be in an Alonso system.

There were question marks in the centre of the park, but that was with neither Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo starting. Alonso was pleased by the sound of Chelsea fans singing the Argentinian’s name again, even if it was drowned out by deafening boos from the home faithful still bearing a World Cup grudge. “Football is emotional, we have to accept in this situation,” said Alonso, keen to move forward with Fernandez in the fold. He now looks likely to stay put this term barring more late transfer drama, while only injury will prevent Caicedo from marshalling Chelsea’s midfield, as it did at the Cottage.

But there remains one glaring issue that continues to plague Chelsea, from manager to manager, system to system. Alonso’s Premier League return was nearly not so fruitful due to the body between the sticks.

It was another nightmare display from Robert Sanchez, whose trademark howlers put points at risk. Josh King’s equaliser, which Sanchez bafflingly let through at his near post, had an xG of 0.07 - the lowest of any goal scored this weekend. He then let the hosts back into the game by parrying Timothy Castagne’s strike straight out to Gonzalo Garcia.

open image in gallery Robert Sanchez had another dire outing in the Chelsea goal ( Reuters )

For all the club’s spending, Sanchez remains the problem player, immune to being usurped from the team by a clear-cut replacement. Maybe 21-year-old Mike Penders will provide the goalkeeping solution long craved, though flinging him straight into the team would go against the club’s much-needed move away from the chaos of youth; it didn’t work with Filip Jorgensen last year.

Alonso did not seem ready to immediately lose faith in Sanchez as his No 1 after one bad showing. “It's about the team, it's not about the individual. As I said before, we can adjust a few things. The first goal, we can do better to defend, we can do better to avoid, but it's part of the game. We need to accept and to learn from them, and this is going to be a process ... Relax and carry on.”

Patience is required for Alonso’s rebuild. The belief that he must turn last season’s 10th-place team into a title challenger within this season is unfairly ambitious, even if it might be an attitude within the walls of the Stamford Bridge boardroom. Hence there shouldn’t be an overreaction when players underperform in the early days of said “process”. Levi Colwill and Romeo Lavia, a duo whose progress has been disrupted heavily by injury, were two others who left a lot to be desired against Fulham.

open image in gallery Xabi Alonso reiterated the ‘process’ of Chelsea’s rebuild and did not indicate he had lost faith in Sanchez already ( PA Wire )

But with Sanchez, entering his fourth season as first-choice stopper, patience is wearing thin. Chelsea got away unscathed this time, but what about next?

Unlike all previous Chelsea managers under the BlueCo regime, Alonso will have an active say on whether this latest Sanchez horror show sparks late action in the transfer window. Emi Martinez is an obvious and available option, if that decision was made.

However, the manager’s comments and calm demeanour suggest he’ll be against any rash change in personnel at this stage. That may turn out to hamper his project in its all important first year.

In the opening scene of American writer Kim Stanley Robinson’s “The Ministry for the Future,” a heat wave combined with a breakdown of the electrical grid in India kills 20 million people. The devastation causes the world's nations unite to combat climate change.

Scientists have long warned that the world will experience more intense extreme weather events like heat waves, storms, floods and droughts. But what once seemed like the realm of fiction is now discussed as a possibility, even an inevitability.

Warning about an “extreme of extremes” or the “Other Big One,” a play off the California reference of a big future earthquake, can be fraught. After all, nobody can say for sure when a weather catastrophe may happen. But in the last few years, the planetary ingredients needed for a massive disturbance have been building. And alarm is growing.

“The risk is that people just think you are exaggerating,” said Daniel Swain, a climate scientist with the California Institute for Water Resources. “It's the ‘Boy Who Cried Wolf’ problem. Sometimes wolves are real. If it’s outside the door, wouldn’t you want to know?”

The risks have been building for over 150 years

In the 1850s, while living in Seneca Falls, New York, amateur scientist Eunice Newton Foote did a series of experiments that put different substances, including carbon dioxide and moist air, inside glass cylinders and left them in the sun. What she found was extraordinary: cylinders with carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that is released when coal, gas or oil is burned, heated up faster and took longer to cool after the sun went down.

Fast-forward: Today, Earth is being heated by massive amounts of greenhouse gases being pumped into the atmosphere, leading to a gradual rise in average global temperature. That increase, 1.44 degrees Celsius (2.59 degrees Fahrenheit) warmer in 2025 compared to the early 1800s, leads to more frequent, and more intense, extreme weather events.

The country that has released the most greenhouse gas, and thus contributed most to climate change, is the United States. But don't expect recognition of that, much less major government-led efforts to combat it, as the country marks its 250th birthday. President Trump has called climate change “the greatest con job ever," referred to climate policies as a “Green New Scam” and U.N. climate predictions were made by “stupid people.”

At any given time there are numerous extreme weather events happening around the globe. Indeed, some have already been so big that we have arguably entered an age of extremes.

Consider Australia's “Black Summer” of wildfires in 2019 and 2020, when 19 million hectares (over 46 million acres) were scorched. Or Pakistan in 2022, when flooding left a third of the country under water. Or Hurricanes Milton and Helene in 2024, which ravaged parts of the southern United States. That is to say nothing of periodic smaller disasters, such as last year's Texas floods that engulfed young campers; the Los Angeles wildfires that chewed through entire neighborhoods; and Typhoon Kalmaegi, which walloped Vietnam and the Philippines.

Sarah Perkins-Kirkpatrick, a climate scientist at Australian National University, says she had a “come to Jesus moment" when she realized that constant extreme weather events wouldn't stop even if the world could immediately reach net zero, the point when as much greenhouse gas is taken out of the atmosphere as released into it. Many countries and major companies have net-zero targets for 2050 or beyond.

Because carbon dioxide can last hundreds of years, and so much has already built up, the damage could take centuries to reverse. And we keep adding more.

“It's the issue of the frog in the boiling water," said Perkins-Kirkpatrick. "If we get used to bracing ourselves, are we going to notice?”

What's clear is that no country is truly prepared for a major climate disaster, and the risks are changing.

Robinson, whose book was published in 2020, says if he were writing today he would include a chapter on wildfires, which have become larger and more destructive. And while the potential heat disaster he writes about in India would arguably be less likely today, thanks to less reliance on the grid and use of solar power, Robinson believes the risks of catastrophe have increased.

The book, he says, “still has a purpose."

open image in gallery The Bug Fire burns near Doyle in unincorporated Lassen County, Calif., Aug. 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Noah Berger, File)

It's basic psychology to avoid talking about uncomfortable things. Climate change, depressing and overwhelming, falls into that category.

Instead of taking action by radically reducing greenhouse gas emissions, or updating our infrastructure to live in a world altered by extreme weather events, a common response, from governments to individuals has largely been to ignore it. Part of the challenge is the care scientists must take when discussing extreme events.

It's impossible to say, for example, that a disaster will happen in a certain year or even decade. But modeling improves every year, and the amount of time between extreme events is shrinking.

Sonia Seneviratne, is a Swiss climatologist who vice chairs a working group of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, the top U.N. body of climate scientists. Seneviratne likens the risk to smoking and lung cancer. People who smoke won't necessarily get lung cancer, but the chances are higher and doctors should say that. Similarly, the risk of massive extreme events rises with every tenth of a degree.

“If such an event happened, I could already see the criticism of people saying, ‘Climate scientists didn’t tell us,’" Seneviratne said. "But we did.”

While earthquakes are not connected to climate change, the way many cities in earthquake-prone California have prepared for a potential Big One is as an example of what's possible. Central to that effort has been Lucy Jones, a seismologist and author of “The Big Ones: How Natural Disasters Have Shaped Us (and What We Can Do About Them).”

In 2014, Jones, then with the U.S. Geological Survey, worked with Los Angeles Mayor Eric Garcetti's administration in developing an initiative that produced widespread retrofitting and earthquake preparedness in LA, and then later in other California cities. Two years later, she formed a nonprofit that advises on preparing for earthquakes and other disasters.

Jones says people will make changes if they believe risks are real and solutions are possible. Without that belief, the response will likely be to ignore the issue.

“Climate denial is one way of coping," said Jones. She said people rationalize by thinking, 'I won’t believe it’s true, so I’ll feel safer.’”

open image in gallery Victims of the unprecedented flooding from monsoon rains use a makeshift barge to carry hay for cattle in Jaffarabad, a district of Pakistan's southwestern Baluchistan province, Sept. 5, 2022. (AP Photo/Fareed Khan, File) ( Copyright 2022 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

Over the last quarter century, many movies have focused on extreme weather events, which provide action and danger to any plot. The cinematic portrayals usually have one of two endings: everything will be okay or we are doomed.

Consider two popular climate movies that came out 15 years apart. In the 2004 “The Day After Tomorrow,” Jack Hall, played by Dennis Quaid, is a climate scientist who, speaking at a U.N. climate conference in Delhi, urges a major reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, warning that a failure to do so will lead to major extreme weather events.

“The climate is fragile," says Hall.

“The economy is fragile,” responds the U.S. vice president.

Shortly after, the disaster that Hall warns about happens. Melting polar ice halts the North Atlantic Current, which moves warm ocean currents northeast across the Atlantic. There are giant cyclones, massive hailstones, heavy flooding and tornadoes before a big freeze takes over — so cold that anybody outside dies.

Eventually the vice president, who has become president, apologizes to the nation for exploiting nature.

“We were wrong," he says.

In the 2021 satire “Don't Look Up,” two astronomers played by Leonardo DiCaprio and Jennifer Lawrence discover a giant comet heading toward Earth. They try to spur action to avoid annihilation. The U.S. president, played by Meryl Streep, isn't interested.

“At this exact moment, I think we sit tight and assess,” Streep says after learning the comet is heading straight toward Earth.

“How big is this thing? Can it destroy my ex-wife's house?” jokes a television news host.

At the end, almost everybody dies, a scenario that even the worst predictions of climate impacts don't envision.

open image in gallery The coal-fired Mountaineer Power Plant, near New Haven, W.Va., operates across the Ohio River from the Lock 24 RV Park and Campground in Racine, Ohio, March 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster, File) ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

As powerful as extreme weather events have already gotten, much worse is likely to come. It’s basic physics.

More than half all greenhouse gases produced by humans throughout history have been released into the atmosphere over 50 years. Those gases create heat, which scrambles weather patterns and ecosystems.

The when of a major climatic event, or more likely several in different parts of the world, can't be known with certainty. A catastrophic event in any given area could be in 50 years, or 10 years, or sooner.

People who deny climate change is real will point out that scientists get projections wrong, and it's true that not every climate model has been correct. But over the last decades, if anything, climate scientists have been too conservative. Climate impacts are happening much faster than predicted.

One of many examples: in January 2022, the U.K. Climate Risk Assessment said there was a 0.02% chance of 40C (104F) or above heat before 2040. That summer, parts of the U.K. topped 40C.

We have also reached a moment when “tipping points" — when deterioration of a given planetary system has crossed a threshold from which it can't recover — are no longer positioned as theoretical or futuristic.

The most commonly cited is corals. According to National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, between 2023 and 2025, 84% of the world's corals suffered the expelling of microscopic algae in response to heat stress, which often leads to dying. Even if temperatures were to sharply drop, the recovery of most corals is doubtful.

The Amazon rainforest, which stores massive amounts of carbon dioxide and helps regulate the climate, is also at risk of a tipping point. Persistent drought, large wildfires and deforestation to make way for cattle have degraded swaths of forest in recent decades. The debate today is when, not if, the Amazon will release more carbon dioxide than it holds.

This year's El Niño, a natural and periodic warming cycle, is expected to be the strongest ever recorded, which could push temperatures even higher, breaking records and leaving damage along the way.

Overall, the Earth is on a dangerous path.

“We need to be talking about some of the worst things that can happen,” said Tim Lenton, climate science professor at the University of Exeter. “It’s natural to think that some bigger shocks are on the way.”

Where Unai Emery is concerned, the silent treatment has taken on a new meaning. The Aston Villa manager’s pre-match interview at Brighton on Sunday was notable for a one-word answer. “Silence,” he said, when asked about Ollie Watkins’ whereabouts. The England striker was absent for the 4-0 defeat, Emery hinting he refused to play.

Watkins appears set on joining Al Hilal. A considerable boost to his bank balance would come with a dent to his reputation. For the nice guy, one of football’s feel-good stories, it surely wasn’t supposed to end like this. When Watkins was playing for Exeter at 21, the riches now offered in Saudi Arabia would have seemed unimaginable. But so, too, would have scoring the winner for England in the semi-final of a major tournament or winning a European trophy. This will be his last big contract – and presumably, much his biggest – but it again invites the question of how much money footballers need.

open image in gallery Ollie Watkins appears set to wave farewell to Aston Villa ( Getty )

Six years at Villa Park should not have left him a pauper. Instead, he may leave Villa with Emi Buendia acting as a false nine at Brighton as they made a false start to their campaign.

A tarnished legacy would be a shame because Watkins and Villa have been very good for each other. He had never played in the top flight before he became their club record signing. He became the only player to reach double figures of Premier League goals in each of the last six seasons. His departure may be drawn out, but perhaps Watkins finished in a way with a match-winning brace against Manchester City, his last game at Villa Park, like his third, an evisceration of Liverpool. There were six goals in his last five games for Villa and, in the one where he did not find the net, they won the Europa League.

open image in gallery Ollie Watkins was a key part of Aston Villa’s rise ( PA Wire )

Watkins etched his name into Villa history; indeed he did so early on with his hat-trick in the 7-2 demolition of Liverpool in 2020. He became the first player since Peter McParland in 1962 to bring up a century of goals for them. That six-decade wait feels all the more astonishing given some of the calibre of players in the intervening period: Brian Little and Andy Gray, Peter Withe and Gary Shaw, David Platt and Dwight Yorke, Dion Dublin and Gabby Agbonlahor.

And yet there have been hints a relationship was frayed and fracturing. Another day when Watkins felt rampant came with the revelation he was angry: he destroyed Newcastle in April 2025 but, in his words, was “fuming” he had been confined to a brief outing in the Champions League quarter-final against Paris Saint-Germain, when Marcus Rashford was preferred. Yet by going now, he would deny himself a chance he wanted then and a role in just Villa’s second European Cup campaign since 1983.

open image in gallery England’s Ollie Watkins scored a memorable winner as England beat the Netherlands at Euro 2024 ( PA Wire )

He was of interest to Arsenal in January 2025 and then Manchester United the following summer, suggesting either or both of a capacity to earn admirers with his performances or an active agent.

Now the timing of Watkins’ wanderlust risks plunging Villa into decline. Perhaps the last week has been a tipping point in a summer that always promised some change. Villa may be stripped of six of the Europa League final starting 11.

Examine them and each case is different. For a club who have breached financial regulations, Morgan Rogers was always the likeliest candidate to command a sizeable fee and Villa got a huge one, in £117m. Youri Tielemans had a release clause, but still produced a £35m profit. Lucas Digne’s departure had seemed an annual possibility and finally happened. Villa tired of Emi Martinez and signed a replacement, Zion Suzuki, before the goalkeeper had even gone.

open image in gallery Unai Emery's Aston Villa squad has been torn apart this summer ( Getty )

But Villa surely did not bank on two others jumping ship. Ezri Konsa represents a fine price, with £51m for a defender who is almost 29. Like Watkins, though, he was a stalwart, a graduate of the lower leagues who became part of the core Emery inherited, this group signed by either Steve Bruce, Dean Smith or Steven Gerrard who were the constants amid the frantic trading.

John McGinn and Tyrone Mings could feel lonely, as the last survivors of that group, if the exodus continues. The purpose of the senior professionals has seemed to underpin the Emery era, helping them to recover from the tougher spells. Now that collective will be no more.

And if, in reality, Villa needed to get younger, suddenly they are being stripped of the certainties experience provided; in Watkins’ case, that included a guarantee of goals, with at least 16 in each of the last three Premier League campaigns. Brian Madjo’s superb Super Cup performance against PSG offered hope for a future beyond him but Tammy Abraham’s ineffectual 2026 is a reminder Emery’s recruitment at Villa has been decidedly mixed.

open image in gallery The emergence of Brian Madjo feels key to Aston Villa if Ollie Watkins departs ( Reuters )

It is one cause for concern if Watkins is going. But even before then, it is the way he seems to be going.

Over seven million 10p pieces featuring the King’s portrait are being released into general UK circulation for the first time, and will soon begin appearing in everyday pockets and wallets nationwide.

The Royal Mint confirmed that 600,000 coins bearing a 2023 date alongside 6.5 million carrying a 2026 date are being distributed across the country to meet a heightened demand for the 10p denomination.

Entering public use from August 25, this marks the initial occasion that 10p coins showcasing Charles’s image have gone into circulation. They represent the fourth coin denomination to feature the monarch’s portrait, following the progressive introduction of 5p, 50p and £1 coins since 2022.

open image in gallery The new coins will be available through post offices and bank branches (Royal Mint/PA)

UK coins bearing the portrait of Queen Elizabeth II remain legal tender and in active circulation, with the aim of ensuring a smooth transition with minimal environmental impact and cost.

With Charles coins representing just 1% of the 24.142 billion coins in circulation across the UK, the new 10p coins will be highly sought after, the Mint said.

open image in gallery (Royal Mint/PA)

The new 10p coins feature the capercaillie bird on the reverse or “tails” side.

The design is part of a collection inspired by the flora and fauna of the British Isles, reflecting the King’s passion for conservation.

The coins will be available through post offices and bank branches.

Rebecca Morgan, director at the Royal Mint, said: “This is a landmark moment for the nation’s coinage, as people begin finding the very first 10p coins bearing the King’s portrait in their change.”

open image in gallery (Royal Mint/PA)

She said of the capercaillie bird appearing on coins: “We hope that by putting this extraordinary bird into millions of pockets and purses, we can spark a nationwide conversation about a species at real risk of vanishing from Britain forever.”

Some 10p coins will also be available at tills in the Royal Mint Experience, the Royal Mint’s visitor attraction based in South Wales.

A recent report from banking and finance industry body UK Finance found that a significant number of people still rely on cash.

It said around 1.4 million UK adults mainly use cash for their day-to-day spending, but 19 million use cash once a month or less frequently, reflecting a wide variation in people’s payment preferences.

Cash use fell to 3.9 billion payments in 2025, down from 4.3 billion the previous year, UK Finance said.

The report said that cash represented 8% of payments in 2025, falling from 9% in 2024 and 45% in 2015.

By 2035, cash use is expected to account for just 4% of payments made in the UK, with around two billion transactions, according to UK Finance.

Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron were part of a long list of women waiting for Katie Taylor to call, but the call never came. It was not a shock when they were both ignored ahead of Taylor’s retirement party – in front of 80,000 at Croke Park in two weeks – but a fight between Mayer and Cameron themselves was a nice idea.

This Saturday, in Birmingham, they fight each other with three world-title belts on the line, and it is one of the very best fights that could be made in the women’s game. It is an MVP promotion, their second in the UK, and once again the full card is exceptional. This time, American stars face Britain’s own in every bout.

Mayer holds the WBC and WBA belts at super-welterweight, and Cameron has the WBO version, which means there will be a decent scuffle at the end between the commissioners in the ring, all desperate to attach their bauble to the champion first.

In an ideal boxing world, Cameron would be getting her third fight with Taylor, and Mayer (who first fought for a world title at super-feather, a full 24lb below this weekend’s limit) would be fighting at a lighter weight.

The women’s game often throws up odd fights at strange weights, and this is certainly one of the very best ever in that category. The willingness and ability of the top fighters to flip in and out of alien divisions has made the women’s side of the sport so competitive.

American Mayer and Britain’s Cameron are both senior members of the team, exceptional fighters, veterans of long and successful amateur careers, and have been in close to 25 world-title fights in five divisions as professionals. They have taken risks, taken hard fights on the road, and are now firmly established as two of the very best in their sport.

open image in gallery Cameron during her brutal second fight with Katie Taylor ( Getty )

Cameron held a version of the world title at lightweight nine years ago, which is nearly 20lb below the super-welterweight limit. It can often feel like there are three weight classes: those under super-feather, then somewhere near the super-welterweight limit, then those up at middleweight and above. Small, medium, and big, if you like.

Mayer has lost just twice, both tight decisions and both in Britain; Cameron’s only loss was in the rematch with Taylor in Dublin in 2023. They could, once Taylor retires at midnight in two weeks, be fighting for the unofficial crown of the world’s top female boxer. Mayer against Cameron feels that big.

Caroline Dubois defends her two lightweight world championships on the same bill and is a contender for that same honorary title.

On Saturday night, there will be no time for getting a sense of distance, feeling their way into the fight or taking a few rounds to – as we say – “have a look”. It will be furious from the start. They can both box, but this fight will be decided by the tiniest margins; if either boxer decides to move her feet, pick her punches and show their ring skills, they risk getting lost in the storm.

Once the first bell sounds, they will meet in the centre of the ring. It will stay that way throughout the 10 short rounds. The pattern of the fight is simple to predict, the outcome with any confidence less so. A draw is a great suggestion; a split decision is almost inevitable.

The US trial of a former Libyan intelligence operative accused over the 1988 Pan Am Flight 103 bombing has been delayed after fresh evidence came to light, a federal judge ruled on Monday. Defence attorneys requested time to review the material in the case, which spans nearly four decades.

Jury selection was due to start on Wednesday in Washington, D.C., for Abu Agila Mohammad Mas’ud Kheir Al-Marimi, in what will be the first trial held in the US regarding the attack on 21 December 1988.

An order issued by U.S. District Judge Dabney Friedrich did not elaborate on the nature of the newly revealed details. Al-Marimi’s legal team said prosecutors disclosed the evidence on Saturday, adding that their "constitutional and ethical obligations require the defense to investigate this development."

A status hearing in Washington has been scheduled for 1 September to discuss the case.

Al-Marimi is charged in the US with building the bomb that destroyed the aircraft, killing 270 people, mostly Americans. Flight 103 was travelling from London Heathrow Airport to John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York when the device exploded in the forward cargo area 38 minutes after takeoff, 31,000 feet (9.45 kilometres) above Lockerbie.

open image in gallery The artist sketch depicts Assistant U.S. Attorney Erik Kenerson, front left, watching as Whitney Minter, a public defender from the eastern division of Virginia, stands to represent Abu Agila Mohammad Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi, accused of making the bomb that brought down Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988, in federal court in Washington, Dec. 12, 2022, as Magistrate Judge Robin Meriweather listens. (Dana Verkouteren via AP) ( Dana Verkouteren )

The blast killed all 259 passengers and crew members and 11 people on the ground in Lockerbie, where the wreckage destroyed an entire city block. Citizens of 21 countries were killed, including 190 Americans and 43 from the United Kingdom. The passengers included 35 Syracuse University students returning home from a semester abroad.

Prosecutors allege Al-Marimi and others carried out the bombing at the direction of Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi, who was ousted and killed during a 2011 civil war.

Two other Libyan intelligence agents were tried by a panel of Scottish judges on a former U.S. military base in the Netherlands in 2000. The tribunal convicted one official and acquitted the other, but the bombmaker’s possible identity remained a mystery for years.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”



Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.



Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.



There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.



It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

Sports.title: Three points from Chelsea’s win over Fulham as Enzo Fernandez CAN have future at club and major transfer message sent
Sports.content:
CHELSEA kicked off their Premier League campaign and the Xabi Alonso era with a 3-2 win at neighbours Fulham.

The exciting trio of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers were all on display – and all firing.



But Robert Sanchez’s blunders cost the Blues two goals at the other end.

SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield gives his three talking points from Craven Cottage…



CURSE CANCELLED

Chelsea have grown from last season, it seems.

Last season they would have thrown this away and bottled it with a red card in the second half.



They’ve spent money, they’ve got new players, a new manager, a new system, and it seems like things are different this season.

One of those things that has changed is this supposed No9 curse at Stamford Bridge, and Joao Pedro is the man who is putting an end to that.

His opening goal inside 31 seconds was absolutely sublime, and his assist for Cole Palmer was just as good, just as full of quality.

He showed the type of player he is, the type of complete striker he has become since moving to Chelsea.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And there is clearly no more curse, because he is the one who breaks the spell.

REPLACE ROB & TRUST JOSH

One thing they do need to sort out is Robert Sanchez in goal.

This was a really disappointing display.



Emiliano Martinez is out there – Aston Villa have signed Zion Suzuki. Pay the money!

If you want to be a serious team this season and compete for the title, Chelsea need to get rid of Sanchez and need to sign a serious top-class goalkeeper.

One player who looked like he could compete in this division is Josh Acheampong.

He hasn’t been given too many minutes since he broke through from the Chelsea Cobham academy system – or CNG as it’s now called.

He was brilliant at Fulham.



Among the three defenders, in terms of actually defending, Acheampong was the best of the three.

He’s still young, he can grow into this team, he can develop in this team.

He’s a brilliant young defender who wasn’t given the opportunity to play all that much last season, but I think he should be from now on.



NOT THE ENZ AFTER ALL?

And the last talking point: is there an Enzo Fernandez problem?

He was loudly booed by everyone inside Craven Cottage who wasn’t supporting Chelsea, but cheered by his own fans.

He was okay when he came on, he wasn’t exceptional.

But the reception showed that he can still be accepted at Stamford Bridge.

If he decides he wants to play for Chelsea, that future is still there for him.



What was interesting is that he was benched for Romeo Lavia in the absence of Moises Caicedo.

So it looks like, at this point, Caicedo, Lavia and Reece James are all ahead of him in the midfield pecking order.

That is somewhat concerning.



It’d be interesting to know Alonso’s reasoning – if it’s a personnel thing or if it’s a personal thing between Alonso and Fernandez.

It remains to be seen whether he’ll stay – if he wants to stay – or if that move to Manchester City will happen before the window concludes.

But Chelsea have grown.

A good game, a good win, three goals.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The most exciting front three in the Premier League, for my money, was on display, and it looks that way going into this season.



But they’ve got issues to fix if they want to be competing at the very top and show just how much they’ve grown.

Sports.title: ‘Did you not watch the game?’ – Cole Palmer in cheeky response to Sky Sports reporter after Chelsea’s win over Fulham
Sports.content:
COLE PALMER gave a cheeky response when he was asked how prepared he is for the season after spearheading Chelsea to all three points against Fulham.

The Blues got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to the perfect start as they notched a 3-2 victory at Craven Cottage.



And Palmer, 24, was the star of the show as he bagged what proved to be the winner in the West London derby.

The Chelsea livewire then showed his comedic side when he showed up for post-match media duties alongside fellow goalscorer Morgan Rogers after the final whistle.



Sky Sports reporter Emma Saunders asked: “How ready are you this season?”

Palmer, who was a shock absentee from England’s 26-man squad for the World Cup, replied: “Did you not watch the game?



“I’m only joking. I’m ready. It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot.

“But through the summer and since I’ve been back [for pre-season], I’ve worked extra hard.

“Obviously, I worked on the injuries that I had to prevent them happening again. When I work hard day in, day out, I know the talent I’ve got.

“Normally I’m not really an emotional person. I’m not really too bothered about many things in life. But over the summer I was recharged. I’m ready and I’m hungry.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Palmer grabbed an assist as Joao Pedro wrote his name into the history books in the narrow win over Fulham.

The Brazilian notched the quickest goal on the opening matchday of a Premier League season by finding the net inside 31 SECONDS.

Rogers and Palmer were then on target either side of half-time as Chelsea made a winning start to the campaign.

The former Manchester City talent was restricted to just 24 Premier League starts last term.



A recurring groin problem, first suffered in the warm-up before a 5-1 thumping of West Ham, forced Palmer to miss large spells of the campaign.

And it ultimately cost the attacking midfielder a place in England’s star-studded World Cup squad.

Sports.title: Ruben Dias’ romance with model exposed after she shares videos from Man City star’s BED months after Maya Jama split
Sports.content:
RUBEN Dias’ new romance with a model has been rumbled after she posted videos from his BED.

The Manchester City defender invited Valentina Best, known as Vally, to stay the night at the home he shared with ex Maya Jama until April.



Fans recognised the bedroom decor from Maya’s previous shots and the road outside the modern £4million mansion from a selfie.

The four-bed home’s kitchen and gym also featured — matching snaps in the home’s listing when it was a prize in an Omaze charity draw.



Ruben, 29, and Love Island host Maya, 31, bought the home from the winner just before Christmas last year, but broke up in April.

The final clue for online sleuths was seeing a snap showing the nearby Costa Coffee shop in Alderley Edge, Cheshire.



Dias was first linked to German Vally, 28, in 2024.

She has 170,000 followers online and shares snaps as she travels the world.



The Sun revealed Dias and Maya’s split after sources said the couple had “reached a crossroads” ahead of a hectic summer.

Portuguese Ruben was playing in the World Cup while Maya was facing a busy filming schedule.

Last month Dias told magazine Esquire Portugal he still hoped to find a serious relationship “just like anyone else”.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Joao Pedro makes mockery of No9 curse as Sanchez shows new keeper needed after win over Fulham
Sports.content:
Chelsea might be a little cold, after all.

Joao Pedro got Chelsea‘s season off to the perfect start after just 31 seconds with a delightful chip over Bernd Leno, having been set up by Cole Palmer in a 3-2 win at Craven Cottage.



But with the lead in their hands, Chelsea showed the same signals of distress that we saw under Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior and Calum McFarlane – a lack of discipline and too many silly mistakes.

Josh King bought the scores level with a powerful effort after 23 minutes, but Robert Sanchez should have done better to stop it.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

With Chelsea in need of a goal before half-time to calm things down, enter stage left, Morgan Rogers.

Maxence Lacroix could have got a nose bleed with how high up the pitch he found himself, but instead weaved his way into the box and delivered the ball across the box for Rogers to finish.



With Pedro and Rogers on the scoresheet, it was time for Palmer to join in the action.

Pedro controlled the ball brilliantly and held it up just as well before laying the ball off to his team-mate who slotted through Leno’s legs to give the Blues breathing room and wrap up the win despite another Fulham goal from Gonzalo Garcia.

This is how SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 2

Not again, Rob. Please. Don’t give Chelsea fans another season of this.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Didn’t look assured at the back for the Blues, with some questionable passes out from the back, before a really poor bit of shot stopping for Josh King’s equaliser.

His role in Fulham’s second goal was not so disastrous, but still not good enough as he palmed the ball out to Gonzalo Garcia to score a goal which got Fulham back into the game again.

A few routine catches and saves is not good enough, Chelsea need a new goalkeeper in order to not undermine an otherwise good transfer window.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 8

Made several crucial blocks and clearances, particularly with the score at 1-1 to keep the Blues in the game.

Was probably Chelsea’s best actual defender in the back three tonight, with the other two struggling a little in this system – one of his best performances in a Blue shirt and he should be rewarded with more minutes.



MAXENCE LACROIX – 7

His first competitive game for Chelsea saw him look a little bit unsure of himself on the ball to start with, but he certainly sorted those issues out before half-time with a wonderful assist for Morgan Rogers first Premier League goal in Chelsea blue.

Really grew as the game went on.

LEVI COLWILL – 3

Levi Colwill was perhaps a little fortunate not to be sent off in the opening ten minutes after a poorly timed tackle on Oscar Bobb after mis-controlling a pass from his teammate.



He’s usually such a consistent performer, but tonight really wasn’t his night, and there was a case to be made for him being sent off on a second occasion in the first half too.

He was caught out of position for Fulham’s second goal too, and just looked out of sorts from the off in this game.

MALO GUSTO – 4

The less threatening of Chelsea’s wingbacks, he was far from convincing despite some decent moments.

It was quite a quiet day for the Frenchman, but in his role you want someone loud who is making things happen, and Blues fans will be excited to see Marco Palestra or even Pedro Neto there instead.

JORREL HATO – 6

Was better than Gusto, particularly going forwards, but had some shaky moments defensively, it’s hard to see where he fits in this Chelsea team long term, as he would ideally be the left sided player in a back three, where Levi Colwill plays.



A real mixed bag from the Dutchman.

ROMEO LAVIA – 6

The role of replacing Moises Caicedo is not an easy one to fill.

Got booked after 11 minutes for a bad tackle on Calvin Bassey who was breaking out from the back for Fulham – and walked the tightrope for the rest of the game quite well.

Almost put Chelsea 2-1 up in the first half when his close range effort following a set-piece was denied by Bernd Leno.

REECE JAMES – 6

Was far from the standout performer, but quietly quite good, the captain.



Influences the game in an attacking and defensive dynamic when he is at his best, and wasn’t quite there today, but still showed his quality and stepped up in midfield with Caicedo out and Enzo Fernandez on the bench.

COLE PALMER – 9

Cole Palmer is back.

With so much conversation about Palmer over the summer, an assist just 31 seconds into the new season will do the Chelsea number 10 a world of good.

He was full of confidence after the opening goal, and looked desperate for one of his own, although he was perhaps a little too greedy at times – a lesson he seemed to learn when he was also involved in Chelsea’s second.

Trying too hard can sometimes be the enemy of progress, but not today for ice-cold Cole, whose consistent and overwhelming effort saw him sprint past Joao Pedro and claim a goal of his own in the second half.



MORGAN ROGERS – 7

The new £117million man bagged on his first competitive Chelsea start after some brilliant work from Lacroix, and might have to pay a fee to Cole Palmer for using his trademarked celebration in the aftermath.

He was caught off guard defensively for Josh King’s equaliser, but all was forgiven when he found the back of the net 18 minutes later.

JOAO PEDRO – 9

Number nine curse who?



It took just 31 seconds for Joao Pedro to get off the mark this season, with a delightful chip over the goalkeeper after latching onto Cole Palmer’s through ball.

His assist for Chelsea’s third, as he repaid the favour to Cole Palmer, was full of just as much quality.

A great touch, a great run and a great lay-off showed why he is turning into such a complete number nine.

He thought he had a second late on, but for the offside flag.

SUBS:

ENZO FERNANDEZ (ROMEO LAVIA, 65) – 5

Kept things ticking nicely when he came on, but was far from exhilarating.



He was booed by anyone in the stadium not supporting Chelsea, but that reaction didn’t seem to bother him too much.

PEP CHAVARRIA (JORREL HATO, 65) – 6

Was solid after replacing Hato on the left for Chelsea, with the Blues seeming a little more assured, although the missed Hato’s attacking presence to a degree.

PEDRO NETO (MALO GUSTO, 76) – 5

Didn’t have much time to make a big impact, but did what was required of him in working hard defensively out wide.

GEOVANY QUENDA (MORGAN ROGERS, 83) – 6

An exciting double change saw he and Estevao introduced together, as supposedly the next generation of exciting Chelsea talents in attack, replacing Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He showed flashes of pace and a willingness to defend, and would have been involved in a late Joao Pedro goal, but for the offside flag.



ESTEVAO (COLE PALMER, 83) – N/A

Similarly to Quenda, he didn’t have much time to make an impact, but always looks good on the ball and gets fans up for it.

Sports.title: Fulham 2 Chelsea 3: Cole Palmer back to his best as he, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers win thriller at Craven Cottage
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S front three decided a brilliant game with a performance to send shivers down the spines of their rivals.

But Blues goalkeeper Robert Sanchez had the same effect on his own supporters as another gaffe-filled display helped Fulham play a full part in a classic derby.



There is rarely a dull moment on or off the field at Stamford Bridge.

And if this game is anything to go by, Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea are going to be a brilliant watch for neutrals this season – for good reasons and bad.



In Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and new signing Morgan Rogers, Alonso has potentially the best attacking unit in the Premier League.

All three scored, Pedro after 31 seconds to give the new manager a dream start.

But Sanchez was at fault for Josh King’s equaliser and for the Gonzalo Garcia goal which made it 3-2 after Rogers and Palmer had found the net either side of half-time.

Just like last season under two permanent managers and one interim boss, Chelsea looked incapable of controlling a game.

But unlike so many matches in the chaotic 2025-26 campaign, the Blues were able to hold on for victory.

Chelsea arrived with bad memories of their last visit to Craven Cottage.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Days after the departure of boss Enzo Maresca in January, the Blues had Marc Cucurella sent off in a 2-1 defeat.

As the rain lashed down, the Blues fans aimed X-rated chants at club supremo Behdad Eghbali, who was sitting next to new head coach Liam Rosenior.

Those were dark omens for a sunny summer evening.

When it emerged Moises Caicedo was out injured, the stage was set for a tough evening.

Yet after barely half a minute, Chelsea’s latest new era had the best possible start.



Maxence Lacroix’s clearing header reached Palmer, who helped the ball first time on to Pedro.

The Brazilian’s brilliant chipped finish over Bernd Leno was that of a man brimming with confidence.

The home crowd were understandably dumbstruck, the away fans jubilant.



Yet if they expected their team’s nerves to be settled, they were to be disappointed.

The normally reliable Levi Colwill miscontrolled a routine pass, Oscar Bobb nipped in, and the Blues defender was booked for stopping him running clear.

Romeo Lavia soon followed Colwill into the book for a hefty foul on Calvin Bassey.



Sanchez also gave notice of what was to come.

First the Chelsea ‘keeper let a backpass go out for a corner, then he made an unconvincing save from a King shot.

Although Palmer, Rogers and Pedro remained menacing and were one good pass away from extending Chelsea’s lead, the arrival of the equaliser was no surprise.

Rogers’ failure to go with his runner allowed King to execute a simple one-two with Timothy Castagne.

Sanchez’s positioning looked wrong and his limp-wristed attempt to stop the ball beating him at his near post was even worse.



Chelsea were rattled.

Josh Acheampong, playing instead of the suspended Wesley Fofana, made two crucial challenges to stop the home team going in front.

The visitors regained their composure and Pedro volleyed wide from a Palmer cross.

Leno saved comfortably from Reece James, then less so from Lavia, before Rogers restored the lead.



Palmer found Lacroix with a cute pass and the centre-back dropped his shoulder, beat Jorge Cuenca and pulled the ball back perfectly past Leno into the centre of the area.

Rogers redeemed himself for his part in the equaliser by sidefooting home.

Palmer upped the ante after the break.

After a mesmerising run which deserved a better finish, he made no mistake with his next chance.



Pedro ran from his own half and waited for Palmer to join him.

The Chelsea No10, from a narrow angle, fired through Leno’s legs.



Moments later it was almost 4-1, but Antonee Robinson stopped Rogers capitalising on Jorrel Hato’s surging run and cross.

Instead it was soon 2-3.

Colwill misjudged a cross and Sanchez could only parry Castagne’s shot straight on to the head of Garcia, who did not know much about his debut goal but cared even less.

Every drama needs a villain.

Enter Enzo Fernandez.



He and fellow Argentinian Valentin Barco had been roundly booed earlier in the evening, but Fernandez’s introduction in place of Lavia with 25 minutes to go took the abuse to new X-rated levels.



But some away fans sang their player’s name, despite knowing he would love to be at Manchester City before the end of the window.

After a lull, Fulham went again, with King dragging a shot wide of Sanchez’s right-hand post.

Bassey was booked for diving in the penalty area, then Robinson raced clear of James, only to send his shot over Sanchez but wide.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Chelsea ‘keeper kept out an effort by substitute Ryan Sessegnon and Pedro had a late effort ruled out for offside.

But the Blues are up and running, and it promises to be a fun ride.

Sports.title: Premier League’s 11,000-capacity stadium NOT READY for weekend clash as builders work round clock on new additions
Sports.content:
BOURNEMOUTH builders are working around the clock to get the revamped Vitality Stadium ready for Saturday’s home kick-off against Everton.

The Cherries announced last week their home will be open for business in

time with sections of the stadium closed.



But exclusive SunSport photos show huge lifting machinery still being

used with just five days to go before Everton head to the south coast.

Floodlights at two of the corners of the Steve Fletcher and Ted

MacDougall stands behind the goal have been moved to make way for the

new corners.





The north west and east corners, which are set to hold an extra 800 fans, will not be ready until early in the season.

When one security guard was asked last night if the stadium would be

ready for Saturday he raised his eyebrows and puffed out his cheeks.

And then he smiled: “Of course it will be ready!”

The main cark park and surrounding pathways around the stadium are

full of rubble, iron and concrete fittings that need to be cleared for

safety standards.



Extensive work has been carried out by Bournemouth to meet European

football regulations having qualified for the Europa League for the

first time in their history.

Media facilities have had to be improved for additional overseas TV

and radio commentators, reporters and photographers.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Cherries have also revamped their hospitality suites and laid a new

pitch for the start of the new campaign.



Bournemouth’s billionaire American owner Bill Foley and the board

opted to expand their current home rather than build a new stadium

away from the site.

The Vitality Stadium will grow from roughly 11,300 seats to 20,200

when all the work has been completed by around the summer of 2027.

Bournemouth started their season with a last-gasp 2-1 defeat to Manchester City on Sunday.

Sports.title: Chelsea's electric front three edge out Fulham in pulsating MNF opener
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.

The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.

Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.

If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"

It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's 3-2 victory over West London rivals Fulham, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says he's very happy Cole Palmer is playing with freedom, after the England midfielders' dominant display at Craven Cottage.

Rogers got in on the act on debut with a late run to finish Maxence Lacroix's cross just before half-time, before his flick-on released Joao Pedro to set up Palmer for a third shortly after the break.

Chelsea would have had an easier night despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo without a nightmare performance from goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose mistakes twice let Fulham back into the game.

The Spaniard, whose position as the Blues' No 1 has long been questioned, let Josh King's powerful but saveable drive in at his near post to level matters midway through the opening period before spilling a shot straight into the path of Goncalo Garcia to allow Fulham to make it 3-2.

The first taste of the Alvaro Arbeloa era suggested the Cottagers will play on the front foot regardless of opposition and they created plenty against their west London rivals - but will need to significantly improve their defensive discipline after being cut wide open for each of Chelsea's goals.

On this evidence they will have score plenty too - and could have snatched a late equaliser when Antonee Robinson horribly miscued a chip with Sanchez in no man's land. But anything less than an away victory would have been harsh on Chelsea, who ran out deserved winners thanks to their electric front three.

Arbeloa: If we play like that, we'll win games

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa on Sky Sports:

"It's a new project. Time is something we coaches don't have. But if we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.

"I'm really happy and proud of my players, what I saw from them. This is the way I want to play. And we're going to play [this way] no matter who is in front of us."

Alonso refuses to criticise Sanchez despite errors

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:

"It's not about talking about individuals, their situations. It's about understanding what it takes.

"For sure, the first goal we can do better than that. But it's a process. It's day one. And normally it's easier to learn with three points."

The key moments from Craven Cottage

1: GOAL! Lacroix's header from his own half splits Fulham's midfield before Palmer finds Joao Pedro to open the scoring after just 31 seconds.

23: GOAL! King's powerful drive goes through Sanchez at his near post to level for the hosts.

41: GOAL! Rogers' late run to the back post is found by Lacroix's cross and finished off by the record signing, who is left totally unmarked.

49: GOAL! Calvin Bassey needlessly pushes up and is beaten by Rogers to a flick-on towards Joao Pedro, who tees up Palmer to add a third.

54: GOAL! Goncalo Garcia nets his own debut goal as Sanchez pushes Castagne's effort straight at the summer signing.

65: BOO! Enzo Fernandez is met by huge jeers as he replaces Romeo Lavia after his antics for Argentina against England at the World Cup.

78: BIG CHANCE! With Sanchez off his line, Robinson's attempted chip lands well wide in a huge change to equalise.

82: INJURY? Shortly after telling the bench he needs to come off and pulling up mid-dribble, Palmer is replaced by Estevao.

What's next?

Rate the players...

Sports.title: Champions? Relegated? One to watch? Carra and Neville's season predictions!
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville made their 2026/27 Premier League season predictions on Monday Night Football.

Title winners

Jamie Carragher - Arsenal

A few weeks ago, I thought Man City might have a chance - but it was all around Rodri. If Rodri stayed I'd maybe make a case for them, but without Rodri, I just can't see it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry.

Gary Neville - Arsenal

One hundred per cent Arsenal. They're way out in front. With what they've got already now in defence and in midfield, with the good attackers that they've got, they've got a really good standard, then they're fine.

Top-four finishers

Jamie Carragher - Man City, Chelsea, Liverpool

Man City are better than Chelsea but the European factor can play a huge part. We saw Manchester United last season. It gives them a big lift, Chelsea.

I think Liverpool would want more, but I think just looking at the Chelsea situation, Liverpool where they are right now, I don't see any way they'd be in the top two, and I don't see any way they can mount a title challenge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Newcastle and Liverpool.

Gary Neville - Chelsea, Man City, Man Utd

Chelsea second? Just purely because of the fact that they've got no European football. If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they're only playing 45 games, they're going to amass an enormous amount of points.

That's based upon the fact that they're going to have more free weeks, they're not going to have the injury pressures, they're not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that. I think they'll just edge past Manchester City.

I can't separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea. I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester City and Bournemouth.

Fifth and sixth?

Jamie Carragher - Man Utd, Spurs

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi and Archie Gray believed they were outfought by Brentford but Jamie Redknapp believes that the squad selection was wrong.

Gary Neville - Liverpool, Brighton

Sometimes you look at Spurs going, 'oh, they've spent a lot of money' and thinking 'quite exciting for Spurs fans, they're finally splashing the cash'. But then I look at the team and I think, 'where's it all gone?'

Savinho and Omar Marmoush will make them a lot better, but I just don't know whether they'll pull it together and that's the question.

I know Brighton are a good unit, they're reliable, they're consistent and I think Brentford and Brighton, those two teams this season may just get in there because they're consistent and they know what they're doing and they're well-drilled.

A well-organised, well-drilled team will beat a team of talented players who are still trying to find their way.

European contender?

Jamie Carragher - Brentford

A lot of people say, when you're managing a club like Brentford, which is so well-run behind the scenes and the hierarchy, it makes it easier for the manager. Of course it does - but watching them this weekend, watching them last season...

Brentford haven't got European football, so I think that will be a big plus for them. I really love watching Brentford play, and for me, that was the best performance of the week [their win over Spurs].

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher breaks down Brentford's style of play to put three goals past Tottenham Hotspur.

Gary Neville - Spurs

Relegated

Jamie Carragher - Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland

Why Sunderland? The fact that they've got European football, they're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday. I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder, where they came up and had a really brilliant season, finished high up the table but a lot of the games, like Sunderland, you win by the odd goal.

I'm not saying it's luck but their underlying numbers had them not far away from relegation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Hull and Manchester United.

Gary Neville - Coventry, Hull, Ipswich

I hope that one or two of the promoted sides stay up but I've not got the faith I had last season.

Having watched what I've seen this weekend, I'm going to go for the three promoted teams to go down.

Relegation risk

Jamie Carragher - Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace haven't had a great pre-season. They lost the first game at Everton, which, to be fair, they were actually very unlucky when you look at the chances they had. I know they had Europe last season, but a new manager, new in the Premier League, lost a few players, still in Europe... I'd probably go Crystal Palace to have a scare.

Gary Neville - Fulham

Watching Fulham [against Chelsea], that's a risk, that's a big risk. Young players, splitting your centre-backs like that, being open...

Top scorer

Jamie Carragher - Erling Haaland

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Erling Haaland has shocked fans and Pep Guardiola after showing off a surprise new haircut ahead of the start of the new Premier League season.

Gary Neville - Erling Haaland

Impact signing

Jamie Carragher - Mateus Fernandes, Spurs

I really liked Mateus Fernandes last season at West Ham and I thought there might be another few teams in for him, better teams than Spurs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arsenal's new number 39! Bruno Guimaraes is revealed to the Gunners fans ahead of their pre-season friendly against Borussia Dortmund at The Emirates Stadium.

Gary Neville - Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal

He's the best signing by a mile.

If you take a player out of Arsenal's team anywhere, probably David Raya is the other one, but in the outfield parts of the pitch, there isn't a drop-off between the first and second choice anywhere, apart from Declan Rice. There's a massive drop when Declan Rice moves out of the team. If Rice gets injured for three months, that would be a risk to Arsenal.

The signing of [Bruno Guimaraes] removes that risk.

He is a massive personality. A different player than Rice but you talk about personality and character on the pitch... he is a brilliant personality. He believes he can win every single football match for his team. He believes he can tackle, he's aggressive, he's somebody you'd want alongside you...And by the way, £75m compared to some of the others that have gone for more is value in this market.

Player to watch

Jamie Carragher - Jeremy Jacquet, Liverpool

He's played one Premier League game and he's only played one pre-season game for Liverpool. [Jeremy Jacquet] looked really good in both games but you know sometimes when you look at a player and they just look the part.

I think this is the first season where a player alongside Virgil van Dijk is going to have to play his own game and at times look after Van Dijk.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Fulham’s match against Chelsea in the Premier League.

Gary Neville - Morgan Rogers, Chelsea

When you're a £120m player you've got to hit numbers. You've got to be 12, 15 goals, you've got to be 10, 12 assists or else you're going to come under pressure.

We know he's a good player, Morgan Rogers. We'd all like him at our clubs. But £120m? Wow.

If he can deliver this season for Chelsea they can go and push Arsenal.

Manager to watch

Jamie Carragher - Matthias Jaissle, Newcastle

He's only young but he's got that little twinkle in his eye. I think Matthias Jaissle will be a fiery character in the Premier League. He's coming to Newcastle, a huge football club, and put in that performance [on Sunday]. I think he's got something about him.

Gary Neville - Xabi Alonso, Chelsea

If he gets the recruitment right and he keeps the players in those front areas of the pitch and he sorts the defence and the goalkeeper out he could be the emerging manager - out of that five that are below Mikel Arteta that are trying to win the league - he could be the next one to win the league

I think this season is critical for him because he's got to finish second or a good third because if he doesn't, without European football, with that squad that he's amassed, then there would be questions.

He's the manager of Chelsea - that means that he basically makes the final decision on transfers, on recruitment. If he goes and does one or two pieces of business in this next week or so, he's got to look after himself and demand that he gets that one or two players in this next week and we know where those areas are.
